api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.AnnounceReaso.summary: Enum AnnounceReason Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll Why an assistant is about to speak on its own (Gesture.Announce). public enum AnnounceReason Fields Other = 0 Timer = 1 A timer it set rang (with a text, it is a reminder). Watch = 2 Something it was told to watch happened («avísame cuando se cierre…»). Message = 3 One of the user's commands or events asked it to say something («Asistente: decir»).

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.AssistantActi.title: Enum AssistantActivity | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.AssistantActi.summary: Enum AssistantActivity Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll What the module is busy with, besides its state: what a character may show it doing. public enum AssistantActivity Fields None = 0 Nothing in particular (or nothing to tell). Other = 1 Something not listed here: a tool of the user or of an MCP server (Tool). Command = 2 Running, finding or explaining one of the user's K-Desktop commands, or an event. Apps = 3 Opening, closing or controlling a program or a window, or ending a process. SearchingWeb = 4 Searching the internet. ReadingWeb = 5 Reading a web page. OpeningWeb = 6 Opening a web page in the user's browser. Files = 7 Looking for files, or opening one. Notes = 8 Writing down a note, or looking for one. Memory = 9 Remembering or forgetting something about the user. Weather = 10 Looking at the weather. Music = 11 What is playing, or controlling the player. Timer = 12 Setting or cancelling a timer. Watching = 13 Setting a watch («avísame cuando…»), or stopping one. Dictation = 14 K-Desktop writes what the user says where the cursor is (with Listening). Screen = 15 Looking at the screen (reading its text or seeing it). Writing = 16 Rewriting a text: translating, correcting, summing up… Calculating = 17 Doing sums, converting units or money, working out dates. System = 18 Looking at the PC (processor, memory, disks…) or freeing its brain. Remarks New ones may come in later versions: show the ones it does not know as Other.

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.AssistantStat.title: Enum AssistantState | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.AssistantStat.summary: Enum AssistantState Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll States the module tells the assistant about; each assistant shows them its own way. public enum AssistantState Fields Idle = 0 Listening = 1 Its wake word was heard, or its talk key or a long click: it is listening (also while dictating). Thinking = 2 The AI is working on an answer. ThinkingHard = 3 The AI thinks it over, slowly (it asked to, or the user said «think it over»): it may take half a minute. LoadingBrain = 4 Its model is being loaded into memory before it can think (from a few seconds to a minute). NoBrain = 5 The order needed the AI and there is none (no model, or its server does not answer). It comes right before Speaking, which says so: a shrug while it says it. Speaking = 6 AwaitingConfirmation = 7 A yes/no question is waiting for the user (the little window that asks for permission). Busy = 8 Carrying out an order: one of its tools or a command is running (Activity says which). Sleeping = 9

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.EntranceKind..title: Enum EntranceKind | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.EntranceKind..summary: Enum EntranceKind Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll Why an assistant comes onto the desktop (Enter(EntranceKind)). public enum EntranceKind Fields Startup = 0 K-Desktop started, or the user switched the assistant module on: its full entrance. Summoned = 1 The user put it on the desktop (Options, the tray, the panel): an entrance that says «here I am». Reloaded = 2 It was already there a moment ago and comes back at once: a new version, another language, its data started afresh, its process restarted or recovering from a fall, a rebuild with --assistant-dev. Reappear where it was, with no show (what it saved on Reloading, in its data folder).

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.ExitKind.html.title: Enum ExitKind | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.ExitKind.html.summary: Enum ExitKind Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll Why an assistant leaves the desktop (ExitAsync(ExitKind, CancellationToken)). public enum ExitKind Fields Shutdown = 0 K-Desktop is closing, or the user switched the assistant module off: be quick. Dismissed = 1 The user took it off the desktop (Options, the tray, its menu): its goodbye. Uninstalling = 2 It is being removed: the last goodbye (its data folder may be deleted right after). Reloading = 3 It comes back at once (Reloaded): no show; save in its data folder what it needs to reappear where it was (the new one may run in a new process).

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.IAssistant.ht.title: Interface IAssistant | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.IAssistant.ht.summary: Interface IAssistant Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll An assistant: a character that lives on the desktop. The host (K-Desktop's assistant process) loads it from its package, gives it the world and its services, and asks it for gestures; the assistant never sees the AI, the tools, the pipe or K-Desktop. public interface IAssistant : IDisposable Inherited Members IDisposable.Dispose() Remarks One thread. Every member is called on the host's engine thread, and so are the continuations of awaits inside them (the thread has its own synchronization context). No locking is needed; never block it. The host only wakes it when needed. Tick(TickInfo) returns how long it can sleep: an assistant at rest asks for a few ticks per second (or fewer) and draws nothing, which keeps the cost close to zero; while moving it asks for one tick per frame and the host paces it with the compositor. Failures are contained. An exception in any member is logged; several in a row unload the assistant. Only the essentials are required. Attach(IAssistantHost), Enter(EntranceKind), ExitAsync(ExitKind, CancellationToken), Tick(TickInfo), PerformAsync(Gesture, IGestureContext, CancellationToken), SetState(AssistantState, StateDetail) and BubbleAnchor; every other member has a default that does nothing (or says no), to implement when the character has something to show. Properties BodyBounds Where its body is now, in screen pixels: what the other assistants avoid stopping on (Others). Just the body, not its particles, bubbles or effects. Null while it is not on screen. Read after every tick. Without it the host takes the bounds of its «body» hit area. PixelRect? BodyBounds { get; } Property Value PixelRect? BubbleAnchor Where speech bubbles of the module point to (usually the top of the head), in screen pixels. Null when hidden. Point? BubbleAnchor { get; } Property Value Point? Showcase Its own animations for the showcase, read when K-Desktop asks for the list (the «Try» tab of its card). Empty by default: the host's own items (entrances, exits, states, reactions, gestures) are always there. IReadOnlyList<ShowcaseItem> Showcase { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<ShowcaseItem> Methods Attach(IAssistantHost) Called once, right after loading, before anything else. void Attach(IAssistantHost host) Parameters host IAssistantHost CanPerform(Gesture) Whether it can do this gesture now (not asleep in a game, has a way to reach the window…). Yes by default: NotPerformed from PerformAsync(Gesture, IGestureContext, CancellationToken) says no just as well. bool CanPerform(Gesture gesture) Parameters gesture Gesture Returns bool Enter(EntranceKind) Appear (fly in, fade in, pop out of a hole…), according to why it comes (EntranceKind). void Enter(EntranceKind how) Parameters how EntranceKind ExitAsync(ExitKind, CancellationToken) Leave, according to why (ExitKind). The host waits for it (3 s at most; the token fires then) before unloading it. Task ExitAsync(ExitKind why, CancellationToken ct) Parameters why ExitKind ct CancellationToken Returns Task HideSpeech() Hides what ShowSpeech(SpeechText) showed: it has been said and read, the answer was cancelled, or the host's bubble takes over. void HideSpeech() OnExtraAsync(string, CancellationToken) One of the extras of its manifest («lander.manual»…), launched from a command, the panel or the menu. Task OnExtraAsync(string extraId, CancellationToken ct) Parameters extraId string ct CancellationToken Returns Task OnPointer(PointerEvent) The mouse over one of its hit areas (CreateHitArea(string)): entering, leaving, clicks, drags and files dragged onto it. The right button never comes: it opens its menu. void OnPointer(PointerEvent e) Parameters e PointerEvent OnSettingsChanged(JsonElement) The user changed its settings in K-Desktop's Options (values keyed as in its settings.json), or one of the common ones (Common, already up to date). void OnSettingsChanged(JsonElement settings) Parameters settings JsonElement OnSystemEvent(SystemEvent) Something happened on the PC (a window opened, a notification, the user left or came back, a hard scroll…): the moment to react on its own. Current is already up to date. void OnSystemEvent(SystemEvent e) Parameters e SystemEvent OnVoiceLevel(double) Loudness of its voice while speaking (0…1, about 30 times per second): lights or a mouth that follow it. void OnVoiceLevel(double level) Parameters level double PerformAsync(Gesture, IGestureContext, CancellationToken) Performs a gesture. The token fires when the time is up or the order is cancelled ("stop", Escape): stop quickly and return. Never throw to say no: return NotPerformed. Task<GestureOutcome> PerformAsync(Gesture gesture, IGestureContext ctx, CancellationToken ct) Parameters gesture Gesture ctx IGestureContext ct CancellationToken Returns Task<GestureOutcome> PlayShowcaseAsync(string, CancellationToken) Plays one of its Showcase items now, whatever it was doing. Completes when it has finished (K-Desktop waits for it to say so, up to 30 s); the token fires when the user stops it or asks for another: stop quickly. False when it does not know the id or cannot now (it is hidden, it is in the middle of an order). Task<bool> PlayShowcaseAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct) Parameters id string ct CancellationToken Returns Task<bool> SetState(AssistantState, StateDetail) What the module is doing (listening, thinking, speaking…), for the character to show it, and with what: Activity says it is searching the internet, reading a page, looking at the screen… void SetState(AssistantState state, StateDetail detail) Parameters state AssistantState detail StateDetail ShowSpeech(SpeechText) Shows what it says its own way, for an assistant whose manifest says "speech": "own": a balloon of its own, a sign it holds up, words in its cloud… The host calls it each time the answer grows while it is being written (Finished false), with all of it when it is ready, and again with a later Until while its voice is still saying it. Each call replaces the text of the one before. The host still keeps the timing, the voice and the chat: show it until HideSpeech(). Return false when it cannot now (hidden, in the middle of a manoeuvre, it does not fit): the host shows its own bubble instead, for the rest of that answer. Not called while the user chose K-Desktop's bubble for it. bool ShowSpeech(SpeechText speech) Parameters speech SpeechText Returns bool Tick(TickInfo) Advances physics and behaviour, and presents a frame on its surfaces if something changed. Returns the seconds the host may wait before the next tick (it may call earlier: an event, a gesture, RequestTick()). Values at or under FrameInterval mean «every frame». double Tick(TickInfo tick) Parameters tick TickInfo Returns double

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.PointerEventK.summary: Enum PointerEventKind Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll public enum PointerEventKind Fields Enter = 0 Leave = 1 Down = 2 Up = 3 Click = 4 Down and up without moving: a plain click. DoubleClick = 5 DragStart = 6 The button went down and the cursor moved: the assistant is being dragged. api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.Rope.html.summary: Class Rope Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll A rope (cable, hook line, leash) simulated with Verlet integration, in screen pixels like everything else. The start is always held (by the assistant); the end hangs free or is held too (stuck in a window, on a projectile). It only resists stretching, so it sags and goes slack, and it never gets longer than MaxLength while its end is free. Fields TimeStep The fixed step of the simulation (s). public const double TimeStep = 0.008333333333333333 Field Value double Properties Damping How fast it loses its movement: the fraction of speed left after one second is e^(−Damping). 0: none. public double Damping { get; set; } Property Value double End Where its end is. public Point End { get; } Property Value Point EndPinned Its end is held (PinEnd(Point)) rather than hanging. public bool EndPinned { get; } Property Value bool Gravity Gravity, in pixels per second squared (down is +Y). Infinite by default. public double MaxLength { get; set; } Property Value double Overstretch How much further apart its ends are than its length (both held and pulled apart): 0 when it is not. public double Overstretch { get; } Property Value double Points The points along it, from the start to the end. public IReadOnlyList<Point> Points { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Point> Pull What it pulls the end with, towards the start: the direction from the end to the start times Overstretch. Zero while it is slack. api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.Variety-1.htm.title: Class Variety<T> | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.Variety-1.htm.summary: Class Variety<T> Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Assembly KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.dll A set of variants to choose from at random: several entrances, reactions, idle animations or lines, so the assistant does not do the same thing every time. Each variant has a weight (how often it comes up compared with the others) and a cooldown (seconds it rests after being picked). It never picks the same one twice in a row while there is another to choose. Give it a seed in tests to always get the same sequence. public sealed class Variety<T> Type Parameters T Inheritance object Variety<T> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples private readonly Variety<Clip> _happy = new Variety<Clip>() .Add(Clip.Jump) .Add(Clip.Spin, weight: 0.5) .Add(Clip.Backflip, weight: 0.2, cooldown: 120); // rare, and never twice in two minutes // in React(Happy): Play(_happy.Pick()); // only the ones that fit where it stands: Play(_happy.Pick(clip => clip.FitsOnTaskbar || !onTaskbar)); Remarks Safe to use from several threads (the engine thread and a gesture). Constructors Variety(int?, Func<double>?) public Variety(int? seed = null, Func<double>? clock = null) Parameters seed int? Same seed, same sequence (for tests). Null: different every time. clock Func<double> Seconds on a monotonic clock, for the cooldowns. Null: its own (any clock works, as long as it is always the same one). Properties Count How many variants it has. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Items The variants, in the order they were added. public IReadOnlyList<T> Items { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<T> NoRepeat Never the same one twice in a row while there is another to choose (on by default). public bool NoRepeat { get; set; } Property Value bool Methods Add(T, double, double) Adds a variant. public Variety<T> Add(T value, double weight = 1, double cooldown = 0) Parameters value T weight double How often it comes up compared with the others (2 = twice as often as 1). 0 = never. cooldown double Seconds it rests after being picked: no other pick returns it before (0 = no rest). Returns Variety<T> Itself, to chain the calls. CooldownLeft(T) Seconds left before a variant can come up again (0 = ready, or not in the set). public double CooldownLeft(T value) Parameters value T Returns double Pick(Func<T, bool>?) Picks one at random by weight, among those that are not resting and are not the last one. If all are resting, the one that will be ready soonest: something always comes out (use TryPick(out T, Func<T, bool>?) to do nothing instead). public T Pick(Func<T, bool>? allowed = null) Parameters allowed Func<T, bool> Only these (the ones that fit now). Always respected. Returns T Exceptions InvalidOperationException None allowed with a weight above 0. Reset() Forgets the last one and every cooldown. public void Reset() TryGetLast(out T) The last one picked (or marked with Use(T)); false if none yet. public bool TryGetLast(out T value) Parameters value T Returns bool TryPick(out T, Func<T, bool>?) Like Pick(Func<T, bool>?), but returns false (and picks nothing) when all the allowed ones are resting. public bool TryPick(out T value, Func<T, bool>? allowed = null) Parameters value T allowed Func<T, bool> Returns bool Use(T) Marks a variant as just done although it was not picked here (it happened another way): it becomes the last one and starts resting. Nothing happens if it is not in the set. public void Use(T value) Parameters value T

api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.html.title: Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk | K-Desktop
api/KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk.html.summary: Namespace KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk Classes AssistantStates CaptionButtons The minimize, maximize/restore and close buttons of a window, when they can be found. CommonSettings The settings every assistant has the same way (Common). Gesture What the module wants to achieve; the assistant decides how. An assistant that only knows Gesture.Communicate and Gesture.React already works: for the rest the module falls back to Communicate and performs the action itself. Gesture.ActivateWindow Bring a window to the front (perch on it, knock on the door…). Commit when it should happen. Gesture.Announce it is about to say something on its own (a timer that rang, «avísame cuando» that happened, «Asistente: decir»), so it catches the user's eye first: it comes closer to the cursor, waves, blinks… The host waits for it (at most TimeLeft, about 2 s; half a second in «Fast») and then speaks with Gesture.Communicate: end as soon as it is done. Nothing to Commit. Gesture.Communicate The generic one: stay visible while the host shows Text in the bubble. Gesture.GoTo Go somewhere (fly, walk, teleport). Gesture.Mark Leave a mark somewhere for a while (beacon, flag, alarm clock), with an optional label. Gesture.MoveWindow Move a window to Destination. Either move it frame by frame with TryMove(long, PixelRect) and return PerformedSelf (K-Desktop then puts it exactly in place), or call Commit and let the module move it. If Window is maximized it arrives already restored by a previous PressButton(Restore). Gesture.PointAt Point at a window, a point or an area (a spotlight, an arm…). Gesture.PressButton Press a caption button. Call Commit() at the moment of the effect (when the shot hits): the window minimizes right then. Gesture.React A short reaction to how something went. Context says where it comes from, how many in a row and whether it is the first of the day, so the same reaction need not look the same every time. Gesture.Scan Sweep an area (screenshot, reading the screen). Gesture.Typing Pretend to type into a window (keys or text are being sent to it). Gesture.WaitForWindow Something was just opened: wait for its window. Appeared completes with the new window (or null when it does not show up in time). HitShape The shape of a hit area, in screen pixels. HitShape.Ellipse HitShape.Polygon Any polygon (a rotated body, for example). HitShape.Rectangle MonitorInfo A monitor: its bounds, its work area (without the taskbar) and its scaling (1.0 = 100 %). OtherAssistant Another assistant on the desktop (Others). Place A place on the desktop a gesture refers to. Place.Area Place.AtPoint Place.Clock Place.OfWindow Place.Tray The notification area of the taskbar, near the clock (volume, network, power…). PointerEvent ReactionContext The context of a Gesture.React, filled by the host. Rope A rope (cable, hook line, leash) simulated with Verlet integration, in screen pixels like everything else. The start is always held (by the assistant); the end hangs free or is held too (stuck in a window, on a projectile). It only resists stretching, so it sags and goes slack, and it never gets longer than MaxLength while its end is free. It steps itself at a fixed 120 Hz whatever the frame rate, so it behaves the same on any screen. ShowcaseItem One of its own animations, for the showcase: a dance, a trick, the way it plays with a ball… What the host already asks of every assistant (entrances, exits, states, reactions, gestures) is not listed: the host launches those itself. K-Desktop shows these in the assistant's «Try» tab and in the catalog, and asks for one with PlayShowcaseAsync(string, CancellationToken). SpeechText What it says, for ShowSpeech(SpeechText). StateDetail The detail of a state (SetState(AssistantState, StateDetail)). SystemEvent Things that happen on the PC, delivered to OnSystemEvent(SystemEvent) on the engine thread. They are what lets an assistant react on its own (the Lander jumps when a notification appears, goes to sleep when the user leaves…). Current is already up to date when one arrives. SystemEvent.FastScroll The user scrolled hard (several quick notches of the wheel), anywhere. Strength 0…1, positive downwards; Position is the cursor's. SystemEvent.FullscreenChanged SystemEvent.HourStruck The clock struck an hour (local time). SystemEvent.MonitorsChanged SystemEvent.NotificationShown A Windows notification (toast) appeared at Bounds. SystemEvent.PauseChanged K-Desktop was paused or resumed. SystemEvent.PowerChanged SystemEvent.QuietModeChanged SystemEvent.RecycleBinEmptied SystemEvent.ThemeChanged SystemEvent.UserIdle No input for Seconds (raised at 60 s and then every few minutes). SystemEvent.UserReturned SystemEvent.WheelTurned One turn of the mouse wheel, only while the assistant asks for them (WatchWheel). SystemEvent.WindowActivated SystemEvent.WindowClosed SystemEvent.WindowMoved A window moved or changed size (raised once it settles, not for every pixel). SystemEvent.WindowOpened SystemState What the host knows about the user and the PC right now. Read it at any time from the engine thread. TaskbarInfo The taskbar of one monitor and, on the main one, the notification area and the clock. Variety<T> A set of variants to choose from at random: several entrances, reactions, idle animations or lines, so the assistant does not do the same thing every time. Each variant has a weight (how often it comes up compared with the others) and a cooldown (seconds it rests after being picked). It never picks the same one twice in a row while there is another to choose. Give it a seed in tests to always get the same sequence. WindowInfo A visible top-level window as the window manager sees it. WorldExtensions WorldSnapshot A picture of the desktop at one moment. Immutable: a new one is made whenever something changes (Changed). Structs MusicBeat The beat of the music playing (Music). PixelRect A rectangle in physical screen pixels (the virtual desktop: every monitor, whatever its scaling). All the coordinates the SDK hands out or takes are in these units. TickInfo Interfaces IAssistant An assistant: a character that lives on the desktop. The host (K-Desktop's assistant process) loads it from its package, gives it the world and its services, and asks it for gestures; the assistant never sees the AI, the tools, the pipe or K-Desktop. IAssistantHost Everything the host offers an assistant. Use it from the engine thread unless a member says otherwise. IAssistantLog Its lines go to K-Desktop's assistant log, prefixed with its id. IAudio Sound. The host mixes everything and applies the user's volume for assistants. IGestureContext What the module gives an assistant while it performs a gesture. IHitArea IKeyboard The keyboard, for assistants with a manual mode (the Lander's game). Reading the state is always allowed; capturing keys makes K-Desktop swallow them so the application in front does not get them as well. ILoop IPointer The mouse. The overlay lets every click through; to be clickable an assistant places hit areas over its body (invisible windows with that shape). Their events arrive at OnPointer(PointerEvent). The right button is the host's: it opens the assistant menu (talk, write, extras, settings…). IRendering Drawing services. The host keeps one transparent overlay over every monitor that never takes the mouse or the focus; each surface is a small canvas on it that the compositor moves for free. ISound ISurface A canvas on the overlay. Call Present(PixelRect, Action<DrawingContext>) only when something changed: the last frame stays on screen (also after the GPU is lost or comes back from a full-screen game), so an assistant at rest presents nothing and costs nothing. IWindowServices Moving and changing windows from the assistant process. IWorld The desktop as the host sees it. Enums AnnounceReason Why an assistant is about to speak on its own (Gesture.Announce). AssistantActivity What the module is busy with, besides its state: what a character may show it doing. AssistantState States the module tells the assistant about; each assistant shows them its own way. CaptionButton EntranceKind Why an assistant comes onto the desktop (Enter(EntranceKind)). ExitKind Why an assistant leaves the desktop (ExitAsync(ExitKind, CancellationToken)). ExtraState How one of its extras shows in its menu and its panel (SetExtraState(string, ExtraState)). GestureKind The gesture names, as listed in the «gestures» of the «traits» of assistant.json (camelCase there: "pointAt", "pressButton"…). GestureOutcome ManoeuvreSpeed PointerCursor PointerEventKind Reaction ReactionSource Where a reaction comes from. ShowcaseGroup Groups of the showcase for an assistant's own animations (ShowcaseItem). SurfaceLayer Where a surface goes in the stacking order of the overlay. WindowCommand What TryCommand(long, WindowCommand) does to a window.

en/assistant/brain.html.title: Brain (the AI) | K-Desktop
en/assistant/brain.html.summary: Brain (the AI) The assistants understand you with an AI model. It runs on your PC with llama-server (from llama.cpp), or on another server you already have, such as Ollama, llama-swap or LM Studio. Settings → Assistant → Brain. Note Without any model the assistants still work: fixed phrases (the time, timers, notes, «remember that…»), your commands and the rules for windows and programs need no AI. Choose No AI (only rules and your commands) to keep it that way. Where the answer is worked out The page tells you where what you say goes: On this PC What you say never leaves the computer On another computer of your network What you say stays at home On the internet What you say leaves your network Models on this PC Where the models of this PC are → llama-server → Add llama-server…: the llama-server.exe that opens the models. If it has a models folder next to it, it is looked in too. With several, each model opens with the one in its folder or closest to it; otherwise with the usual one (Make it the usual one). Folders with models: the .gguf files inside them are listed. One of them is where the ones you download go (Open, or move it elsewhere). Add model: paste the link of a Hugging Face model or type its name (unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF, or unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF:Q4_K_M for one quantization). Each file says whether it fits your graphics card, is tight or doesn't fit (it will be slow); the biggest one that fits is already chosen. Models that can see images offer their vision part too. The Models list shows those of this PC and of the other servers, the one in memory in green, with Load, Free, Delete and llama-server options for that model only (for example -c 32768 for more context). Other servers Other servers → Add: Ollama, or any server compatible with OpenAI (llama-swap, LM Studio…), on this PC or another, with its address and, only if it asks for one, an API key (stored encrypted for your user). Test says how many models it has. Their models show up in the same list. Choosing the model Setting Model Automatic: the biggest one that fits in your graphics card. Or a specific one, or No AI To think harder Used when you say «think it over», when the model sees it is not enough, or when you tell it it got it wrong. The same model (reasoning before it answers), another model, or Never. With another model, Reason before answering decides whether it reasons first or answers as it is (quicker) Both have Browse… (a .gguf from any folder) and Load when the chosen one is not in memory How long it reasons when thinking harder A little, normal, a lot (only when it reasons). More helps with hard things, but takes longer Unload it after Unused for this long, it leaves memory (or Never: only when you ask). Loading it again takes a few seconds One model at a time Loading one unloads the others. When off, several stay while they fit Vision Models that can see images load with their vision part (it takes a little more) Free the graphics card for games With a game on the whole screen, the model leaves the graphics card. A film does not count. It loads again when you talk to it Each assistant can think with its own model (its card → Basics → Thinks with, and its own one to think harder: Global, The same model or one of the list, with its box to reason or not, and how long it reasons). An assistant's package may suggest a model: the install card and its Basics tab offer to download it (never ticked by default), only if it fits and you do not have it. Freeing the graphics card The model is loaded by itself when you talk to an assistant, and while you are still saying the order. To take it out of memory: Free next to it, at the top of the page; say or write «free the brain» / «unload the model» (and «load the brain» to have it ready); the Assistant: brain action in a command or an event (before a game, a render…). Thinking harder Small models answer in a moment but can get a sum or a riddle wrong. Ask «think it over», «think it through» or «think carefully» (before or after the question), or tell it «that's wrong»: it thinks it over and checks. A big model may also decide to think harder on its own. It takes longer: up to half a minute. Test the model At the end of the page, Test the model gives the model a list of test orders and tells you how many it gets right and how long it takes on average. Nothing is really run. Open the bench opens Assistant\bench.json, to write your own orders.

en/assistant/index.html.title: Assistants | K-Desktop
en/assistant/index.html.summary: Assistants An assistant is a character that lives on top of your windows. It walks or flies around, reacts to what happens on the PC, and you can talk to it: «Lander, minimise Chrome», «Kobii, what's the weather tomorrow?». When it runs one of your commands every step can be seen: the Lander flies over and shoots the minimise button, and the window minimises right on impact. Note The assistant module is optional. While it is off, K-Desktop loads nothing of it and behaves exactly as without it. The assistants Assistant What it is Lander A small lunar module that flies between your windows, lands on them, tows them with a grappling hook, and has its own game (manual mode, missions, races) Kobii A little creature that walks, climbs your windows, plays, eats, sleeps and lets you pet, brush or high-five it Kumo A soft cloud that floats about, wraps windows to carry them, rains, makes rainbows and dances to your music K-Desktop The built-in assistant without a character, for when you want answers without anyone on the desktop Several can be on the desktop at the same time; each one has its own wake word, key to talk, language, personality, voice and even its own AI model. Turning it on and installing one Settings → Assistant → General → Turn on the assistant module. Settings → Assistant → Catalog: each assistant with its clips, what it can do and Install…. You can also open a .kai package with a double click, or use Assistants → Add assistant. The install card shows what it is, what it can do and who signed it, and offers to record its name as a wake word, to create commands for its shortcuts and to download the AI model it suggests. Press Install. A new version installs over the old one and is swapped in live, keeping the assistant's data (%APPDATA%\K-Desktop 5\Assistants\Data\<id>, included in backups). Installed assistants tell you when there is a new version (Settings → Updates): it is always offered, never installed without asking. Signed packages The card says who signed a package: It shows Meaning Verified · name Signed with a key K-Desktop knows (K-Desktop's own assistants) Signed by «name» Signed with another key: the name is only what the package says, but updates must come with the same key Not signed No signature: it installs, with the usual warning (not installed) The signature does not match: something in the package changed after it was signed If an update is signed by someone else than the version you have, the card warns in red. Its card In Settings → Assistant → Assistants, each assistant has its page: Put on the desktop / Hide (Activate / Deactivate for K-Desktop). Basics: its wake word, its key to talk, the model it thinks with (and the one to think harder), and the settings every assistant shares —size, volume, liveliness (how much it moves on its own), and whether it can be picked up with the mouse— plus «Always use K-Desktop's bubble». Personality: another language and personality for this assistant. Voice: who speaks (Kokoro, Piper, Windows…) with only that engine's settings, its profile, and its own speed and volume. Try: the assistant on a small pretend desktop of its own, doing each thing it can show (its animations, entrances and exits, states, reactions, gestures, what it does to a window). Nothing of it touches your desktop. Below, in another row, its own pages (from its package): the Lander's game options, Kobii's colour… What is not changed stays Global: what is in Settings → Assistant for all of them. Panel → Assistant shows each assistant with what it is doing and its model in one line, and two tabs: Conversation (the chat, its Activity —what it did, with undo; Everyone shows everyone's— and the technical details) and …'s panel (scores, achievements, buttons), which shows also when it is not on the desktop. Talking to it How Its wake word «Lander, …». Recorded in its card; each assistant has its own Its key to talk Hold it and speak (each assistant can have one) Long click Hold the left button on it for half a second and speak Writing Middle click on it, or Write to … in its right-click menu, opens a box; or the chat in Panel → Assistant Phone The Assistant tab of the web app, written or spoken Commands Assistant: ask sends it a text (or opens the box to write); the answer can be said, pasted over the selection, copied, shown on a sheet or kept in {result} Its right-click menu has Write to …, its own actions (extras), its panel, its settings and Hide. Dropping files on it (from the Explorer) opens a small window: «What do I do with "file"?», with suggestions by type (summarise or read a document, describe an image or read its text, summarize an audio or turn it into text, see what is in a folder, open it…) or your own words. What happens when you ask Fixed phrases go first, without AI: «what time is it?», «set a timer for 10 minutes», «remember that…», «open youtube.com», «what's playing?», «weather tomorrow», «free the brain»… They answer in a moment. Your commands: if what you said names one of your commands clearly, it runs (with its gestures). Otherwise the AI answers, choosing among its tools the ones that fit. Risky things (closing programs, deleting files, shutting down) ask first with a small window, by voice too («yes» / «no» / «yes, and don't ask again»). Settings → Assistant → General → Ask before doing something sets it: never, only risky things, or the first time. Gestures and speed Settings → Assistant → General: Manoeuvres: Showy, Normal or Fast (under half a second). Animate up to N actions of a command (the rest run without gestures, except window ones). Also show the commands you run yourself: commands launched by hotkey, menu or voice are also shown as gestures, as decoration.

en/assistant/memory-knowledge.html.title: Memory, notes and documents | K-Desktop
en/assistant/memory-knowledge.html.summary: Memory, notes and documents The assistants keep three different things, each with its page in Settings → Assistant: What it is You say Memory What they know about you: your name, what you like, important dates «remember that my boss is called Luis» Notes What you ask them to note down for you «note that I have to buy milk» What it knows Your documents: folders and files they read so they can answer with what they say «what does my contract say about the deposit?» All of it stays on your PC, and all the assistants share it. Memory «Remember that…», «keep in mind that…», «don't forget that…» saves it at once, without depending on the AI. «What do you know about me?» / «What do you remember about me?» tells you the most important things. «Forget that…» / «forget about…» removes it (and can be undone). Learn from what you talk about: after each chat they note what is worth remembering. Each memory says where it came from: You asked, Learned while talking or You wrote it here. On the page you can Add something you want them to know, Edit or Delete each memory, or Clear all. When an order fits something they remember, they use it: «when I say "the usual", I mean my Work command». Notes «Note that…», «write down…», «make a note to…» saves a note; «what did I write down?» or «read me the shopping list» finds them. They also change them by voice: «take the milk off the shopping list», «add eggs to the list» (a list one per line or all in one line, «Shopping: milk, eggs and bread», keeps its shape), «delete the note about the plumber» (if several fit, they ask which one; anything can be undone from the activity). On the page you can add, edit and delete them. A long answer on the reading sheet can be kept as a note with Save as a note (see Long answers). What it knows (your documents) Add folders (Add folder…) or single files (Add files…) with your documents —notes, manuals, contracts, invoices…— and the assistants answer with what they say and tell you where it comes from. They are read once on this PC and kept an eye on: a new or changed file is read again by itself. Nothing leaves the computer. What is read: text and Markdown, PDF, Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), web pages, subtitles and e-mails (.eml), and code or data files that are not too big. With Read pictures and scanned PDFs on, also pictures and PDF pages without text, with Windows' text recognition (it takes longer the first time). What is not allowed: a whole drive, or folders of Windows or of programs. Hidden folders are skipped, and so are a project's library and build folders (third_party, vendor, build, dist…), the folder of styles and scripts of a saved web page (Page_files) and package version lists (package-lock.json…); minified code is left with No text. While it reads the page shows «Reading: 412 of 1,300 files», roughly how long is left and the file it is on (in a big one, also which piece). It reads gently and pauses while a full-screen game is on, while K-Desktop is paused and while an assistant is answering. Reading speed: Gentle, Normal or Fast (faster uses more of the PC). Pause reading stops it until you press Resume reading (what was already read is still used). Each folder or file has Open the folder and Remove; folders also have See the files: the list, in its own scroll, with each file and its pieces, pages, or why it could not be read. You can search by name or folder (wildcards too: *.pdf, *.c *.h, 2026/*, src/**/*.c) and filter (Read, Not read yet, No text or unreadable, Taken out). Each file can be opened, shown in its folder or taken out of what it knows (not read, and what was read is forgotten; Put back brings it back). A folder on a drive that is not connected keeps what was read. Try a search: what an assistant would find if you asked it this, and how long it took. Read it all again and Forget it all (your files are never touched). It searches by words and by meaning: «how much did I pay for electricity in October» finds the October bill even if it says «power supply». The meaning part uses EmbeddingGemma, downloaded with the voice models (Settings → Voice); without it, it only finds what you ask with the same words as the document. When nothing in your documents answers, the assistant says so instead of making something up. Files you give it Dropping files on an assistant (or asking about one) is different: they are read just for that order, without adding them to What it knows. See Dropping files.

en/assistant/tools.html.title: Tools | K-Desktop
en/assistant/tools.html.summary: Tools Tools are what the assistants can do when you ask them something: set a timer, find a file, read a web page, close a program… For each order only the few tools that fit reach the AI, so it chooses well even with hundreds of them. Settings → Assistant → Tools shows all of them —built-in, yours and each MCP server's— with a search box. Open each group to switch off the ones you don't want, choose when it asks before doing it (Without asking, The first time, Always) or Test it with a small form. Everything an assistant does shows in Panel → Assistant → Activity (its own, or everyone's with Everyone): what, how (rule, command, AI, memory…) and whether it worked. What can be undone has an Undo button (or say «undo that»). Built-in tools Subject Tools For example Commands Run your commands · Find your commands · Explain a command · Check a command or event · Look at the log · See your statistics · Teach voice phrases · Run an event · Create an event · Stop a countdown «turn on game mode», «when I open Steam turn on game mode», «what does the backup command do?», «why didn't the eight o'clock event run?», «what failed yesterday?», «which command do I use the most?», «when I say telly run my TV command», «don't shut down the computer after all» Time, reminders and maths Time and date · Timer · Cancel a timer · Program an order · See what is pending · Remove something programmed · Tell me when something happens · Stop watching · Date maths · Calculator «remind me in half an hour», «at seven empty the recycle bin», «tell me when the download finishes», «how many days until christmas» Notes and memory Save a note · Find notes · Change a note · Delete a note · Remember something about you · Forget a memory «note that I have to buy milk», «remember that my boss is called Luis» Files Find files · Open a file · Read a file · Turn an audio into text · Delete a file · Move a file · Write a document · Copy a file · Create a folder · Compress into a ZIP · Extract a ZIP · Search your documents «find the electricity bill pdf», «open the last thing I downloaded» Internet Open a website · Search in the browser · Look it up online · Read a web page · Check the network · Send to the phone «how much is an RTX 5080», «summarise this page», «is there internet?», «is the NAS answering?», «send this address to my phone» Screen and texts Look at the screen · Translate and fix texts · Read what is copied · Search what was copied before · Copy a text «what is this error», «translate what I copied into French», «what have I copied?», «find the link I copied this morning», «copy the plumber's number for me» Programs and PC Open a program · Handle windows and programs · See the open windows · Arrange several windows · Force close · PC status · Free the brain · Change the volume · Change the audio device · Screen · Light or dark mode · Wi-Fi and Bluetooth · Lock the PC · Shut down or restart · Take a screenshot · Power plan · Keep awake «minimize Steam», «put the browser and VS Code side by side», «set the volume to 30», «turn on dark mode», «lock the PC», «Chrome is not responding, force it closed», «why is the computer slow» Music and video What's playing · Control playback «what song is this», «pause the video» Weather and conversions Weather · Convert units and currencies «will it rain tomorrow», «how much is 50 dollars in euros» Some details: Tell me when something happens watches for a program closing or a window appearing, the processor or the graphics card calming down, a download finishing or a folder that stops changing. The assistant that set it says it when it happens, and, if you ask («tell me on my phone…»), it reaches your phone too. Send to the phone sends a text, a link or a small file to your paired devices (all, or the one you name). It asks the first time, as Ask before doing something says. The calendar, the mail and Telegram have their own tools (checking and changing the agenda, reading and sending mail, writing and reading Telegram): see Calendar, Mail and Telegram. Create an event: «when I open Steam turn on game mode», «if I leave the PC alone for 10 minutes, lock it», «every time I connect the headphones tell me their battery», «when a pdf arrives in Downloads, let me know». It makes an event of any kind (a time, a program that opens or comes to the front, the PC left alone, locked or waking up, a file in a folder, a USB stick, headphones, a controller or a screen, the network, the battery or the processor above or below a %, sunrise or sunset, when K-Desktop starts…) and saves it at once: it runs your commands (also when it ends, like when you close the program) or asks the assistant something, with an «Only if» of hours, days or an open program if you say so. It asks like the riskiest thing it will do (your commands, once), says what it made, shows in Events marked with the assistant that made it, and «undo» removes it. Program an order: «at 19:00 check the weather, send it to me on Telegram and shut down the computer», «tomorrow at 9…», «every day at 8…». It is kept as an event that, at its time, gives the order to the assistant as if you said it then. What it will need is approved when you ask (it asks once, for the riskiest part, as Ask before doing something says); at that time it asks nothing: it does what was approved and what needs no permission, and nothing else. Shutting down or restarting always goes last, and at the end it says what worked and what didn't. If the PC was off or asleep at that time, it is not done late: it is removed and you are told. «No need for the seven o'clock thing» removes one. «What do you have pending?» answers everything at once: timers, programmed orders and what it is watching for you («tell me when…»). A plain reminder for another day («remind me tomorrow at 7…») is a timer. Look at the screen reads text with Windows' text recognition (also «copy the text of this window»); to understand a picture it needs a model with vision. Translate and fix texts works on what you have selected or copied (translate, correct, summarise, more formal, a list, shorter…) and pastes it back in the same window or leaves it copied. Your clipboard is put back as it was. Read what is copied reads what is in your clipboard: the text; if you copied files, which ones (and it can read them); if it is a picture, it looks at it like Read a file (with a model that sees, or its text by Windows' recognition). Search what was copied before looks at the texts of the clipboard history (never pictures nor files), and with Copy a text it can give you one of them again. It is turned off in Settings → Clipboard → Assistants can read it. Copy a text leaves one ready to paste (undoing it brings back what was there, while K-Desktop stays open: what is copied is never saved to a file). As what is copied may be a password, another program never reads it (nor the history) through «Share the tools» with «Only what looks things up», and with «Everything, asking you first» you are asked. Look it up online searches the web and reads the first useful result; Search in the browser only opens the search in your browser. Change the volume, Change the audio device, Screen (brightness, project like Win+P, turn the screens off), Light or dark mode, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, Lock the PC, Shut down or restart (also sleep, hibernate and sign out), Take a screenshot, Power plan and Keep awake do the same actions as your commands, without you having to make one. They ask like those actions and as Ask before doing something says: shutting down, restarting, sleeping or signing out always; turning off the screen, the Wi-Fi or the Bluetooth, the first time; locking, never (nothing is lost). Shutting down and restarting wait 10 seconds you can cancel. Arrange several windows places two to six open windows together on one monitor (where the first one is, or the one you say): side by side, one above the other, in a grid, or one big on the left and the rest on the right. An assistant on the desktop carries them one by one, as when it moves one window. See the open windows tells which ones you have, where they are and which are minimized. Check the network tells whether there is internet and, when there is not, where it fails (no network, the router, the DNS, a sign-in page like in a hotel); whether a machine or website answers (by its name, its address or «the router», also a port: «server:22»); your local and public IP; and the Wi-Fi you are on, with its signal (Windows only gives the signal if desktop apps may use your location). Weather uses Open-Meteo and currencies the European Central Bank's rates (no account needed). Without a city it uses Settings → Assistant → General → Where you are, or Windows' location if you allow it. Turn an audio into text («summarize my latest recording», or an audio you drop on it) turns what is said into text with K-Desktop's voice model (without AI), and the assistant summarizes it or answers about it. Without saying which, it uses the newest recording in the Record audio folder. It leaves the text in a .txt next to the audio; if there was one already (for example, from When it ends, transcribe it), it reads it without transcribing again. Delete a file sends it to the recycle bin; it and Move a file always ask first (a move can be undone). Write a document creates a text file (.txt unless you say another kind; also .md, .csv, .json, .html…; never .bat, .ps1 or programs) on the desktop or where you say. If there is one of that name it is not touched: they ask whether to replace it, and replacing always asks on the PC. Copy a file, Create a folder, Compress into a ZIP and Extract a ZIP never write over anything (the copy or the zip is called «name (2)», and a zip is always extracted into a new folder). Everything can be undone: what was made goes to the recycle bin and a replaced document gets back what it had. Check a command or event tells why it does not work or did not run, without running anything: whether it is turned off, whether the program or folder it opens is missing, whether it calls a command that no longer exists, whether its «Only if» is met now, its last runs and the times it did not run (K-Desktop notes the reason: an «Only if» not met, paused, a time missed with the PC asleep…). Look at the log answers «what failed yesterday?» or «did the eight o'clock event run?», and See your statistics, «which command do I use the most?». Your own tools (JSON) A JSON tool gives the assistants something new to do without compiling anything: switch on a Home Assistant light, send you a Telegram message, run one of your commands with phrases of its own, chain several steps or launch a script. They are in %APPDATA%\K-Desktop 5\Assistant\Tools\, one .json per tool (Tools → Custom → Open folder, or New from a template). They reload a moment after you save, add or remove one. Schema: tool.schema.json. With "$schema" pointing to it your editor shows the mistakes as you type. A file with errors is not loaded and K-Desktop tells you why. Examples of every type. { "name": "living_room_light", // lower case, numbers and _ (mcp_ is reserved) "type": "http", // http · kdesktop · routine · script "description": "Turns the living room light on or off.", // for the model "examples": ["turn on the living room light", "living room off"], "parameters": { "state": { "type": "string", "enum": ["on", "off"], "description": "on or off" } }, "intent": "turn the living room light {{state}}", // what you see in the activity and when it asks "say": { "ok": "Living room light: {{state}}.", "error": "The hub is not answering." }, "risk": "safe", // safe · askOnce · askAlways "readsOnly": false, "gesture": "waitForWindow", // optional: waitForWindow · tray · clock · typing "timeout": 15, "request": { "method": "POST", "url": "http://homeassistant.local:8123/api/services/light/turn_{{state}}", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {{secret:ha_token}}" }, "body": { "entity_id": "light.living_room" } } } description is for the model: what it does and when to use it. Models follow English best, but any language works. examples: phrases that ask for it. They decide which tools reach the model for each order. If you say exactly one of them and the tool needs nothing from the model, it is done at once without the AI («good night» → a routine). parameters: what the model has to give it (string, number, integer, boolean, with enum, default, minimum, maximum). Those without default are required unless required says otherwise. A wrong value is explained to the model, which can fix it. say: what the assistant says when it is done. Without it, the model says it in its own words. readsOnly: it only looks something up (a temperature, a state); the model answers with what it returns. risk: safe never asks; askOnce asks until you say «Yes, and don't ask again»; askAlways always asks. gesture (optional): what the character does meanwhile —wait for the window it opens, go to the tray, leave a mark by the clock, type in the window in front—. Only decoration: the tool does not wait for it. Placeholders Placeholder What it is Where {{parameter}} The value the model gave Everywhere {{secret:name}} A secret (see below) URL, headers, body, a script's arguments and environment {{result}} The answer (or the part chosen with pick) say {{result.field}} A field of the JSON answer (attributes.temperature, items.0.name) say {{status}} HTTP status or the script's exit code say In a JSON body, a text that is only "{{parameter}}" keeps its type: a number stays a number. Types Type What it does http Any web API: request with method (GET by default), url, headers, query, body (or bodyText with contentType) and pick (the part of the answer given to the model). An error status (4xx, 5xx) is a failure kdesktop One of your commands with phrases of its own: "command": "Cinema mode", by its exact name (never a similar one). Risky commands ask as always routine Several steps: another tool (built-in or JSON, never another routine) with its arguments, one of your commands ("command"), or a wait ("wait": 1, up to 30 s). A failing step stops the routine unless it has continueOnError script One of your scripts: "script": { "file": "check.ps1", "args": ["{{host}}"], "env": { "API_KEY": "{{secret:my_key}}" } }. .ps1 (Windows PowerShell), .bat/.cmd, .py (with uv run --script if you have uv, otherwise py or python), .js (Node.js) or .exe. They run as your normal user (never as administrator), without a window, 30 s at most; what they print is the answer and an exit code other than 0 is a failure Important A script always asks before its first run, even with Ask before doing something set to Never. With «Yes, and don't ask again» it is approved; if the script or its .json changes, it asks again. A script that turns up in the folder without you knowing never runs unseen. Secrets Passwords, tokens and keys your tools and servers use: Tools → Secrets, or in %APPDATA%\K-Desktop 5\Assistant\secrets.json. Written in plain text there, each value is encrypted with your Windows user the first time it is read. The model never sees a secret: it is only put in when the request is sent, and hidden as ••• if an answer contains it. A backup restored on another PC cannot read them: write them again. MCP servers An MCP server is a program (or an address) that gives several tools at once: the same ones Claude Desktop, VS Code or Open WebUI with mcpo use. Tools → MCP servers: Import… reads another program's file (mcpo's config.json, Claude Desktop's) and lets you choose. Paste takes the JSON block you copied from a server's instructions. Variables that look secret (*_TOKEN, *_KEY, *_SECRET, *PASSWORD*, CHAT_ID…) become encrypted secrets. Servers for things the assistants already do (files, screen, clipboard, memory, time, the web) come unticked, with the reason. Add server: a program (node, npx, uvx, an .exe…, its arguments and folder) or an HTTP address; its variables or headers, each normal or secret; the longest wait per call and after how long unused it stops. Each server has its own page with its state, Start and test, and its tools to switch on or off (the assistants choose better among fewer). They are started by the assistant process, as your normal user, only when one of their tools is needed, and stop on their own after some minutes unused; Tools → Running now shows which are running. Their tools are remembered, so choosing among them never starts a server. By default they ask the first time, except those the server says only read. What a server writes to stderr goes to Logs\mcp-<server>.log. From a command With the Assistant: use a tool action, a command uses any of these tools without the AI: with a shortcut, from a QuickMenu or in an event (for example, pausing downloads when a game opens). What it gives back goes to {result} for the next actions. As the command is yours, it does not ask first, except for a script that is new or changed or a tool you set to Always; if the command runs by itself, those are not done. It needs the Assistant module on. Sharing with other programs The other way round: Tools → Share turns the assistants into an MCP server for Claude Desktop, VS Code, Open WebUI or any program with MCP. Switch on Share the tools and Copy the configuration, then paste it into the program's MCP settings (claude_desktop_config.json, VS Code's mcp.json, mcpo's config.json): { "mcpServers": { "k-desktop": { "command": "C:\\…\\KDesktop.exe", "args": ["--mcp"], "env": { "KDESKTOP_MCP_KEY": "…" } } } } What they can use: Only what looks things up (the time, sums, the weather, finding files or searching the internet, reading the screen… nothing that changes anything), Everything, asking you first: what changes something asks on this PC with the usual window, even if you set the assistants not to ask, or Everything, without asking: only what you set to Always asks (and a new script, the first time). With Ask for the key (the default) only the programs with the key get in; Change the key leaves out those that had the old one. Off, any program of yours on this PC gets in (never from another PC or user) and the copied configuration carries no key. K-Desktop must be open with the assistant module on. Each call shows in the activity with the program's name, and the page shows who is connected. Tools you switched off, and those of your own MCP servers, are not shared.

en/assistant/voice.html.title: Voice and conversation | K-Desktop
en/assistant/voice.html.summary: Voice and conversation Besides the bubble, the assistants answer aloud, each with its own voice. The natural voices download once and work without internet. Settings → Assistant → Voice. To talk to them you use K-Desktop's speech recognition (wake words, a key to talk…): see Voice and Talking to it. Who speaks Language they speak to you in: they answer in that language even if you talk to them in another one, and the voices offered are of that language (K-Desktop's, or one of the six). Engine Automatic Kokoro; otherwise Piper; otherwise the Windows voices Natural voice (Kokoro) The most natural one. English, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese (not German yet). About 325 MB, plus half a megabyte per voice Natural voice (Piper) Voices in every language, from 20 to 115 MB each; high-quality ones sound better (low-quality ones are not offered) Windows voices No downloads. There are more in Windows Settings → Time & language → Speech Beeps only Don't speak (bubble only) Speed and Voice volume are on the same page. The voices of each engine (downloading and choosing them) are in Voice → Voices: Kokoro Folders with your voices: voices you already have (.pt or .bin, with their Kokoro name, like af_bella; the language comes from the first letter) are used from there without downloading them, marked as yours. One that is also in the list shows only once. K-Desktop never deletes anything there. Kokoro voice and Mix with: two voices mixed make a new one, halfway between them (How much of …). Piper voice and its Variant (some voices have several people or ways of speaking). Folders with your voices: Piper voices you already have (.onnx with its .onnx.json) are used from there without downloading them, and K-Desktop never deletes anything there. Delete the unused ones frees space. For some languages Kokoro, and Piper always, need espeak-ng (GPL licence, 9 MB), downloaded separately with the voice. Windows voice: which of the ones Windows has. Try this voice, under each one: the test sentence with that voice, as it is (no effects). How they sound How they sound: each assistant brings its own profile (the Lander talks over the radio, from the Moon), or choose one for all: Natural, Classic robot, Martian, Mission control, 8-bit, Beeps, or one of yours. Try it: choose who says it and how it says it (normal, happy, after a failure) and press Try. Voice profiles Voice → Voice profiles is the list: the built-in ones and yours, with New at random and Import…. Pressing one opens its editor on the same page (← Voice profiles goes back to the list), with Duplicate, Export and, if it is yours, Delete. The built-in ones stay as they are: Duplicate one to make yours. The Use for everyone icon (in the list and in the editor) puts that profile in How they sound (lit while everyone uses it; pressed again, or if you delete it, each assistant goes back to its own). The profile's Voice only counts if Who speaks is Automatic. A profile has a voice (engine), speed and volume, and a chain of effects its voice always goes through, in order (drag them by the dots to change it): Effect Pitch Higher or lower Formants The size of the mouth, without changing the pitch Ring modulator Classic robot Vocoder Synthesizer robot, on one note Bitcrusher 8-bit robot Radio Narrow band and static, with a beep at the end and a click when opening and closing Chorus Metallic, wavering voice (martian) Flanger Like chorus, faster and deeper: jet plane Echo From a cockpit (short) to space (long) Glitch Cuts and repeats, as if broken Besides Always, a profile can add effects for some moments, such as when the assistant is happy or after a crash. Try it when something changes lets you hear each change as you make it. Profiles can be exported and imported (.json). When they speak aloud Keep quiet with something full screen: with a film or a game in full screen, only the bubble. Quieter at night: from 22:00 to 8:00, the voice at half the volume. They sound from where they are: louder from the speaker on the side where the assistant is. While an assistant thinks and answers, the volume of the other programs stays down (with Turn the volume down while you speak), and it does not take its own voice for an order. Each assistant its own On each assistant's card, Personality and Voice: Language: the one it answers and speaks in. By default the one in Settings → Assistant → General → Language they speak to you in (they answer in it even if you talk to them in another). Personality: what tells the AI who it is and how it talks. Change it as you like (Reset brings back the one of its package). Voice: engine, voice (only the chosen engine's), profile, and speed and volume of its own, or «Global». Try its voice. K-Desktop itself (the assistant without a character) has the same pages. The conversation Fixed phrases need no AI: «stop» / «never mind» cancels what it is doing; «repeat that»; «undo that»; «repeat the last command». Questions back: if it asks you something («Chrome or Edge?») after a spoken order, it listens a few seconds for your answer, without the wake word. Permission by voice: when something asks first, answer «yes», «no» or «yes, and don't ask again». «Think it over» makes it think harder; «that's wrong» makes it check again (see Brain). While it thinks it may say «One moment» if the answer takes a little. «Write what I say» starts dictation: what you say next is typed where the cursor is. Everything is in the chat of Panel → Assistant, whichever way you said it, and a Stop button. Long answers When you ask for something long («explain it in detail», «make me a list», «write me an email», «summarise…») or the answer does not fit a bubble, it says only a short summary and writes the whole text on a reading sheet next to it. There you can Copy it, Save as a note, or have it read to you (Read it to me / Stop). Continue in the chat opens the chat window with that assistant. In the chat, Read it all opens it again. The «Assistant: say» action In a command or an event, Assistant: say makes an assistant say something in its bubble and aloud, without the AI («The backup has finished»). Before saying something on its own —a timer, a «tell me when»— an assistant first catches your eye (the Lander flies to the mouse, Kobii walks up to it); with this action, only if Go towards the mouse before saying it is ticked. With Keep quiet with something full screen in its voice settings, while something is full screen on any monitor only the bubble shows. To have it read what you select, write {selection} as the text and give the command a hotkey: select a text in any program, press the hotkey and the assistant reads it with its voice. A long text is read whole: the bubble shows its start and the whole text stays on its reading sheet, next to it. You cut it like any other answer: «stop», «be quiet» or another order. If nothing is selected, a notice says so.

en/index.html.title: K-Desktop | K-Desktop
en/index.html.summary: K-Desktop K-Desktop turns any key, mouse button or combination into a sequence of actions: open programs, arrange windows, change the volume, take screenshots, call Home Assistant, type text, read text off the screen… The same commands can be launched from a menu at the mouse, a search box, your voice, your phone, the network, or automatically when something happens on the PC. On top of that, the optional assistant module puts characters on your desktop that you can talk to. They think with a local AI model, carry out your commands with gestures you can see, and come with tools for files, the web, the screen, music, timers, notes and your own documents. Warning K-Desktop 5 is used every day but is still under active development: things change from one version to the next. What is in this documentation K-Desktop Installing it, commands and their actions, QuickMenus, the launcher, events, macros, K-Board, voice, the phone and the settings Assistant module Assistants on the desktop: installing them, their brain (the AI), their tools, memory and documents, and their voices Making assistants For developers and artists: assistants without code (pictures and JSON) and with code (C# and the SDK), signing and publishing them SDK API reference Every type of the assistant SDK In a few words Commands: actions bound to shortcuts (CTRL + ALT + O, Mouse 5, CTRL + Wheel Up…), globally or for one program. QuickMenu and launcher: a menu at the mouse and a search box that find and run everything. Events: «when this happens, run these commands» (a time, a program opening, the PC idle, a USB drive…). Macros and K-Board: record keyboard and mouse, remap keys and buttons per program. Voice: your own wake word, recognition on your PC (no internet), dictation. Phone: a web app and an Android app with your commands, a touchpad, a keyboard and the assistants' chat. Five languages: English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. Private: speech, voices and the AI run on your PC. See Privacy.

en/k-desktop/actions.html.title: Actions | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/actions.html.summary: Actions Every action a command can run. Add them with Add action in the command editor; they run in order. Open and run Action What it does Run application Opens a program, file, shortcut or script, as the normal user or as administrator. Open folder Opens a folder or a special Windows location. Open web page Opens a URL in the browser of your choice. Control application Activates, closes, keeps on top or waits for an application by its process name. Run script Runs a CMD (BAT), PowerShell or VBScript script written right there. Windows Action What it does Window Maximizes, minimizes, places (halves, quarters, thirds), centres, moves to another monitor or to the next or previous zone (layouts) or makes a window transparent. Window layout Puts each program in its zone of one of your layouts. Always on top (on/off) Pins the active window above the others, or releases it. Keyboard and mouse Action What it does Send keys / text Sends a key combination, types text or moves the mouse. Clipboard Copies a text (with date, time…) or changes the one there: plain, upper case, lower case, clean links… and pastes it. Or opens the clipboard history. Play macro Plays a recorded macro (keyboard and mouse with their timing), once or several times. K-Board Turns a K-Board profile (remapped keys and buttons) on, off, or toggles it. Dictate Types what you say where the cursor is, without AI. Ends after a few seconds of silence, with Esc or by saying «stop dictating». Sound Action What it does Volume Sets, raises, lowers or mutes the volume: of the speakers or the microphone (the default ones or one you choose), one program or the one in front. Audio output Changes the default sound device. With several chosen, each run switches to the next one. Audio input Changes the default microphone. With several chosen, each run switches to the next one. Play sound Plays a sound chosen in a panel by kind (alerts, alarms, calls, system and yours) with K-Desktop's and Windows' sounds, which play when clicked, or another file (.wav, .mp3, .wma, .m4a, .aac, .flac). The ones you put in your sounds folder show under «Yours». Media Plays, pauses, skips to the next or previous one, or stops, with Windows' media controls (Spotify, browsers, Media Player…): in what is playing or in a program you choose from the ones that have something now. A player that does not show up gets the media keys. The OSD shows the song that plays. Record audio Records what the PC plays, the microphone or both, or saves what just played (Settings → Audio recording). With When it ends, transcribe it, it turns what is said into text (without AI, with the voice model) and saves it in a .txt next to the audio; the command waits (Esc stops it) and leaves the text in {result}, so an Assistant: ask can summarize it. Screen Action What it does Record video Records to MP4 a region you pick with the mouse, the active window or the mouse's monitor, with what the PC plays, the microphone, both or no sound. A pill at the top shows the time, Pause and Stop, and is not in the video; the same hotkey (Start / stop) or the tray also stop it. In Format it can also be a GIF or an animated WebP (much lighter): no sound and 30 seconds at most (it stops by itself; the pill says how much is left). When it stops, the file is in {resultado}. Frames, quality, pointer, clicks and folder in Settings → Screen recording. Screenshot Captures a region you pick with the mouse, the active window, a monitor or all of them; copies it and saves it. With Annotate first an editor comes first: arrow, box, text, highlighter, blur (what is covered cannot be read), crop and copy text (drag over some text, or click for the whole picture: the Windows OCR reads it and copies it without closing the editor), with seven colours, a thickness to choose and Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y; keys 1–7 pick the tool). From there Copy or Save (what you press counts that time). Esc cancels and the command does not go on. Copy text from the screen Reads the text of a region you pick with the mouse, the active window or a monitor and copies it. No AI: Windows' text recognition (OCR). If you cancel the region (Esc) or it finds no text, the rest of the command is not run. Colour picker Freezes the screen with a magnifier by the mouse; a click copies the pixel's colour as #1E90FF, rgb(30, 144, 255) or hsl(210, 100%, 56%) (your choice). The arrows move the mouse one pixel and the wheel changes the zoom; Esc cancels and the rest of the command is not run. Ruler Freezes the screen and measures in pixels: moving the mouse, the distance between the edges around it (up to where the colour changes); dragging, a box. A click copies «width × height»; Esc cancels. Magnifier A lens (rectangular or round) that follows the mouse and enlarges what is around it, or the whole screen it is on. Screen Turns the screens off (all or the ones you choose), changes the projection (Win + P), the brightness, or a monitor's resolution and refresh rate. Panel Shows, hides, locks or unlocks one of your panels, or all of them. Windows theme Switches Windows and the apps to light or dark mode, or toggles between them. Network and internet Action What it does Web request Sends an HTTP request (GET, POST…) without opening the browser: Home Assistant, APIs, phone notifications… Wake a computer Turns on another PC or a server over the network (Wake-on-LAN) and, if you want, waits until it answers. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Turns the Wi-Fi or the Bluetooth on, off, or toggles it. Send mail Sends a mail from one of your accounts, with text with variables and attached files, or leaves it as a draft. See Mail. Send via Telegram Sends you (or a contact), by the bot or the account, a text with variables, a file, a screenshot or what is on the clipboard. See Telegram. Create event Adds an event to a calendar, at a time or in a while. See Calendar. Join the meeting Opens the Teams, Meet or Zoom link of the current or the next event. Send to phone A text, a link or a small file to your paired phones or browsers (all, or the one you choose), as a notification. With variables. See What the PC sends. System Action What it does Files and folders Copy, move, rename, delete (to the recycle bin or for good), create a folder, zip, unzip or make a backup: sync (only what is new or changed, optionally removing from the destination what is gone) or a dated copy each time keeping the latest. The source is a list of files, folders or patterns (C:\Music\*.mp3) typed in or added with the buttons. The destination may be inside the source: it never copies itself. Progress shows on the OSD (Esc stops it) and the next action can wait until it is done. Hidden files (on/off) Shows or hides hidden files in Explorer. Power plan Switches the Windows power plan (High performance, Balanced…) or goes to the next one. Keep awake The PC does not sleep (and, if you want, the screen stays on) for some minutes, while a program is open or until you turn it off. While it lasts a cup shows in the tray, with «30 more minutes» and «Let it sleep». Closing K-Desktop lets the PC sleep as usual. Power Shuts down, restarts, sleeps, locks or signs out, with a cancellable countdown. Flow Action What it does If… Checks something (a program open, the time, a device, the network, CPU use, a variable…) and, if it isn't so, stops the command, skips the next actions or runs another command instead. See conditions. Wait Pauses before the next action. Commands Runs, enables or disables another command. Open QuickMenu Shows a QuickMenu at the mouse position. Show message Shows an on-screen message for a while. Show notification A card in a corner with your title, text, picture, colour and sound, for as long as you say. Clicking it can open something (a file, a folder, a web page) or run another command, and the next action can wait until it closes. Its sound can be Global (the one of Settings › Messages and notifications). With something full screen it does what those settings say. Disable in current app (on/off) Disables or re-enables K-Desktop hotkeys in the active application (useful in games). Assistant Only with the assistant module on. Action What it does Assistant: ask Says something to an assistant, as if you said it out loud. Without text, it opens the box to write to it. With the answer: Say it (in its bubble and with its voice), Paste it over the selection, Copy it, Show it on a sheet or Only keep it in {result}. Except Say it, the command waits for the answer (Esc stops it), the assistant neither speaks nor shows its bubble, and the answer is left in {result}. With If it is not on the desktop, it comes out to do it, it comes out when it is hidden. Example: «Translate into Spanish: {selection}» and Paste it over the selection. Assistant: say The assistant says something in its bubble, without the AI. Handy in events: «The backup has finished». With {selection} it reads what you have selected with its voice (a long text, whole). With If it is not on the desktop, it comes out to do it, it comes out if it is hidden. Assistant: chat Opens, closes or toggles a separate chat window, with the same conversation as Panel → Assistant. It starts with the last assistant you talked to in it or with a fixed one. Its icon, at the top, changes the assistant (the ones not on the desktop come out when chosen); the pin keeps it on top and Esc closes it. It remembers where it was, its size, the pin and the assistant. Assistant: brain Takes the AI model out of the graphics card (before a game or a render) or loads it now so the first answer does not wait. Assistant: use a tool Uses one of the assistants' tools without the AI: a built-in one (the weather, converting, reading a web page, the PC's status…), one of your own in JSON, or one from an MCP server (sending a Telegram message, putting something in your calendar, pausing downloads…). You pick it from a list, which leaves out the ones that are already a K-Desktop action, and fill in its data in a form or, with Show as JSON, by hand; variables work in its texts ({selection}, {result}…). What it gives back goes to {result}. It does not ask first, except for a script of yours that is new or changed, or a tool you set to Always in Settings › Tools; if the command runs by itself (an event, at startup…), that one is not done. If it fails, the rest of the command is not run. Example: {selection} in the text of the Telegram tool to send what is selected. Assistant: action Puts an assistant on the desktop, hides it, or runs one of its own actions, like the Lander's manual mode (if it is not on the desktop, it comes out for it or nothing is done, as you choose). Variables: passing data from one action to another The texts of the actions (a message, an address, a text to type, a script…) can have variables. Type { in the field and the ones you can use show up; choose one with the arrows and put it with Enter.
