Variable What it holds {result} What the previous action that gives something gave (see below). {selection} What is selected in the window where you ran the command. It is copied once and the clipboard is left as it was. {clipboard} The copied text. {clipboard:2} What was copied before the last one, from the clipboard history (:3, :4… further back). {date} and {time} Today's date (2026-10-28) and the time (09:30:05). {name} What an earlier action kept with Save in a variable and that name. These give something: Copy text from the screen (the text read), Colour picker (the colour), Ruler (the size), Web request (the answer), Assistant: ask (the answer, except with Say it), Assistant: use a tool (what it gives back), Record audio (what is said, with When it ends, transcribe it), Clipboard (the text it leaves copied), Screenshot (the saved file), Record video (the video, when it stops) and Run script (what it writes, when Wait until it finishes is ticked and the window is Hidden; not in VBScript). These actions have the Save in a variable field: with a name (letters, digits and _), what they give stays available until the command ends, even if another action changes {result} later. Variables last one run of the command. The commands it runs with Commands and the commands of the same event share them. The Spanish names work too ({resultado}, {seleccion}, {portapapeles}, {fecha}, {hora}). Anything else between braces is left as it is.

en/k-desktop/arrangements.html.title: Layouts | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/arrangements.html.summary: Layouts A layout cuts your monitors into zones and says which programs go in each one. Then it puts them like that whenever you want: with a hotkey, from a QuickMenu or on its own, with an event. A layout covers every monitor; one without zones in it is not touched. Place your programs the way you like (the browser on the left, the editor on the right, music on the other monitor…). Layouts → New layout: it already has the windows open now, each one as a zone with its program. Give it a name («Work»). Test puts it now. Create a command that applies it leaves you a command ready to give a hotkey. Save windows replaces the zones of every monitor with the windows open at that moment: each monitor is cut by its windows, and each zone gets the programs of its windows (a maximized one, the whole screen; minimized ones do not count). Zones never overlap: windows one on top of another share a zone, and a wide free area becomes an empty zone. Each program also remembers the exact place and size of its window, so putting the layout leaves everything as it was. Zones At the top of Zones there is a pill per monitor: the connected ones and, faded, the ones that were connected at some point (K-Desktop remembers them), so you can prepare the TV layout even when it is not plugged in. A dot on the pill means that monitor has zones in this layout. Below is the drawing of the chosen monitor: Click a zone to mark it (a click outside the zones unmarks it); another click on the marked one cuts it in two where the dotted line shows (vertically; with Shift, horizontally). Drag the lines between zones to change their size (they stay at a half, a third or a quarter when you pass close). The ✕ on a line joins its two zones, with their programs. Templates: whole screen, 2 or 3 columns, grid, one big and two small, or 2 rows. The programs each zone had go to the new zone where its middle fell. Remove zones leaves the monitor without zones. Under the drawing are the programs of the marked zone, as in K-Board's Only in these applications: type the program or pick it from the list and press Add, or press the cursor button and click its window. A zone without programs is only there to snap windows into. Programs saved with Save windows have a pin: they go to the exact place their window had, shown dashed in the marked zone. Right-click → Fill the zone forgets that place, and the program stretches to its zone, like the ones you add by hand. When it is put If the program is open, its window goes to its zone (or to its saved place, if it has a pin); it does not open another one. A whole-screen zone leaves it maximized. With several windows of the same program (two of Chrome), it tells them apart by their title, else by order. If it is not open, it is skipped, unless Options → Open the programs that are not open is on: then it opens it and places it as soon as its window appears. Microsoft Store apps cannot be opened this way. The notice says which ones were not open. Monitors are recognized by their name, even if Windows numbers them differently. If a zone's monitor is not connected, its programs go to the main one, in the same place. Using it The action Window layout puts a layout from any command. With a Screen plugged in or out event it is applied on its own: for example, a «Movie» layout when the TV is plugged in and a «Work» one when it is unplugged. Snapping windows into the zones Each monitor uses the zones of the layout put on it last (remembered after a restart). A monitor where none was ever put does not snap. Shift + drag: while you drag a window by its title bar, hold Shift and the zones of each monitor show on top; the one under the mouse is marked and, when you drop it, the window fits into it (a whole-screen zone maximizes it). If you let Shift go, the zones disappear and the window stays where you drop it; Esc cancels. It is turned off in Options → Snap with Shift while dragging (it applies to all layouts). Next or previous zone: the Window action has To the next zone and To the previous zone. They follow the zones' numbers and, after the last one of a monitor, go to the next monitor. Options → Create the zone hotkeys leaves you both commands made with Win + Alt + → and Win + Alt + ←. Snapping always fills the zone, even if the program has a saved place.

en/k-desktop/calendar.html.title: Calendar and agenda | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/calendar.html.summary: Calendar and agenda K-Desktop keeps your appointments in one place: calendars of its own, your Google calendars and any .ics address (Outlook, holidays, sports…). It reminds you before each event, fires events, has actions to create events and join meetings, and the assistants can check and change your agenda. The Agenda Agenda, in the side menu above History, is there while some calendar has Show in the agenda. It shows the events, each in its calendar's colour, in two ways: List: the days from today on, with today always at the top (even with nothing on it). The event going on now has Now, and the ones already over are dimmed. Month: the whole month; all-day events are a band in their colour and the rest show their time. The arrows (or the mouse wheel) change the month, +N more opens that day in the list and a double click on a day adds an event on it. Today goes back to today in both. The coloured buttons at the top show or hide each calendar (at least one has to be shown). Also: New event, or a click on one to Edit it (or View it, if its calendar is read-only); right click: Join, Copy and Delete. Join opens the Teams, Meet or Zoom link of an online meeting. Search events…, Show earlier days and Show more days. Update now reads the server calendars again; Import .ics and Export to .ics move events between calendars and other programs. An event has a title, calendar, start and end (or All day), Repeats (daily, every weekday, weekly, monthly on a day or on «the second Tuesday», yearly, every so many of them; for ever, until a day or a number of times), Reminder, location, Meeting link (found by itself in the location or the notes) and notes. Changing or deleting a repeating event asks: This one only, This and following or All of them. An event from a read-only calendar can only be viewed. Calendars Settings → Calendar lists every calendar. Each one has its name (the assistant knows them by it: «put it in Work»), colour, Show in the agenda and a Reminder for new events. Default calendar is where new events go when you do not say another one. New calendar: your own (Work, Family…), kept on this PC and in its backups. Subscribe to an .ics: a read-only calendar from an address, read every so often (15 minutes by default). It is the way to see Outlook, or Google without connecting the account (Where to find the .ics address explains how). The address is kept encrypted: a secret calendar address lets anybody who has it read the calendar. Google: connect the account in Settings → Accounts → Google (calendar only, or read and edit), then Show its calendars and choose which ones. Google asks for your own free application (a Client ID); How to get the Client ID walks you through it. K-Desktop never sees your password: you sign in in the browser. Reminders Settings → Calendar → Reminders chooses How it reminds you: an on-screen message (OSD), a notification (with Join when the event has a meeting link) or an assistant says it (if it is on the desktop; otherwise an OSD). Google reminders here too is off by default, because the phone already gives them. Try a reminder shows one. Actions and events Create event (action) Adds an event at a time or in a while, with title, location and notes that can have variables Join the meeting (action) Opens the link of the current meeting (from 10 minutes before it starts) or the next one Calendar event (event) Some minutes before an event, when it starts or when it ends: from a calendar, with a word in the title, online meetings only, with a location… The commands get {appointment}, {appointment_time}, {appointment_place}, {appointment_notes}, {appointment_link} and {appointment_calendar} 10 minutes before a Work meeting: do not disturb and open Teams. The assistants With the Assistant module, the tools Check the calendar, Add an event, Change an event and Delete an event: «what do I have tomorrow?», «put the dentist on Friday at 5», «move the meeting to 11», «cancel Thursday's dinner». Adding never asks, changing asks until you say «don't ask again», and deleting always asks; all three can be undone.

en/k-desktop/clipboard.html.title: Clipboard history | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/clipboard.html.summary: Clipboard history K-Desktop keeps what you copy (texts, pictures and files) so you can paste it again, and it can be used instead of Windows' own history. Opening it With its hotkey, in Settings → Clipboard. If you set it to Win + V, this history opens instead of Windows' one. From the tray: Clipboard history. From a command or a QuickMenu: the Clipboard action with Show the history. From the launcher: what you copied shows among the results (Enter pastes it). In any text of an action or of Texts, {clipboard:2} is what was copied before the last one (:3, :4… further back). It opens next to the mouse. Type to search and choose with ↑ ↓: Key What it does Enter (or click) Pastes it in the window where you were Shift + Enter Pastes it without format Ctrl + 1…9 Pastes that row Ctrl + P (or the row's pin) Pins it (or unpins it) Del Deletes it from the history Tab Changes the filter: All, Text, Pictures, Files, Pinned Esc Closes it With a right click: paste, paste without format, paste with a change (upper case, lower case, each word capitalised, remove extra spaces, clean links), copy without pasting, open the picture or the files' folder, pin and delete. Options In Settings → Clipboard: Keep what you copy: off, nothing new is kept. From the tray, Pause the history stops it for a while. Pictures: copied pictures too (up to 20 MB each). Assistants can read it: to ask them «what did I copy before?»; they only see the texts. How many to keep (200 by default) and Delete after days (0: never). Pinned ones always stay. Don't keep what is copied in: programs whose copies are never kept; password managers by default. Clear the history: deletes everything but the pinned ones. Privacy It is kept encrypted for your Windows user and only on this PC (it is not in the backups). It never keeps what a program marks as private (password managers do) nor what K-Desktop pastes in passing, like the long texts of Texts. While K-Desktop is paused it keeps nothing either.

en/k-desktop/commands.html.title: Commands | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/commands.html.summary: Commands A command is a list of actions with a name. It can be run by a hotkey, from a QuickMenu, the launcher, your voice, your phone, the network, an event, another command or an assistant. Hotkeys A hotkey is any combination of keys, mouse buttons and the wheel: CTRL + ALT + O, F13, Mouse 5, Mouse 4 + Mouse 1, CTRL + Wheel Up… To record one, click the hotkey box and press it. A command can have several. For one program only: limit the command to some programs (by their process name). When the same hotkey exists globally and for one program, the specific one wins inside that program and the global one everywhere else. Disable in: in Settings → Disable in you list programs (games, remote desktops…) where K-Desktop's hotkeys do nothing. The action Disable in current app toggles it for the program in front. K-Desktop warns you when a hotkey is already used by another command, by K-Desktop itself or by an assistant. Hot corners and mouse gestures Next to Add hotkey there are two more buttons: Screen corner: choose one of the four (↖ ↗ ↙ ↘) and the command runs when you rest the mouse there for a moment. Any corner where the cursor stops counts, also the one left loose by a taller or shifted screen; where two screens meet there is no corner. It never fires with a button held or in full screen. Mouse gesture: a drawing of one stroke (←, →, ↑, ↓, C, L, N, S, U, V, Λ, W, M, Z or a circle) made holding the right button (or the middle one, Mouse 4 or Mouse 5). If you click without moving, or hold it still, the button works as always; Esc while drawing cancels it. The gesture window has a box to try the drawings with the left button, and Draw your own: give it a name and draw it three times. The wait in the corner, the gesture button, showing the stroke and the programs without gestures are in Settings → Mouse. Actions Each command has a list of actions that run in order: open a program, place a window, send keys, change the volume, wait, run another command… See the complete list of actions. Each action can be switched off without deleting it, and its order changed by dragging. Run in the editor tries the command at once. A command that takes a while (a wait, a macro, a script it waits for…) shows a ▶ in the list while it is running, and next to the number of commands you see how many are running: click it to see them or stop them all. Run turns into Stop while that command is still running. Two commands cannot have the same name (nor two events, QuickMenus, macros or K-Board profiles): if you type one that already exists, the previous name stays. An action that opens something chooses whether it runs as administrator or as a normal user. If… (conditions) The If… action checks something and, if it is not so, stops the command, skips the next actions or runs another command instead (chosen from the list; it gets the same variables). It can check: Condition Example A program is open / is in front «If Steam is open» A time and days «If it's Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 18:00» A device is connected «If the Xbox controller is connected» The sound plays through a device / something is playing «If sound plays through the headphones» A network «If connected to HomeWiFi», «If there's no network» Battery or mains «If running on battery» A host answers «If 192.168.1.10 answers» A file exists «If D:\backup.lock exists» The clipboard «If the clipboard contains "http"» CPU, GPU or memory use «If the processor is above 80 %» Battery below a % «If the battery is below 20 %» Screens plugged in «If there are 2 screens or more» It is daytime «If it is daytime», «If it is night» (between sunrise and sunset where you are) A text or variable: has something, contains, is equal to, is greater or less than «If {result} contains "error"», «If {result} is greater than 80» Every condition can be turned around with The opposite («isn't», «doesn't»…). When comparing, numbers are compared as numbers («7» is less than «10»; «2,5» and «2.5» are the same) and text without minding upper or lower case. History History lists everything that ran: which command, when, from where (hotkey, menu, launcher, voice, phone, network, event, assistant, MCP server, command line…) and whether it went well. Organising Search by name, hotkey or action, and filter the list: all commands, those in no QuickMenu, or those of one QuickMenu. Enable or disable a command, hide it from the list (it still works), duplicate it or delete it (it also leaves the QuickMenus it was in). Available for remote control: whether the phone and the network can see and run it. Icon: automatic (from its first action), a built-in vector icon in any colour, a Windows icon library, any image or a website's favicon. In the editor, Test only this action runs one action alone. Export and import A command, a macro, a K-Board profile, an event, a QuickMenu, a layout or a text can be taken on its own to another PC (or kept apart) with Export…, from the list's right-click menu. It saves a .kdx file with everything it needs: the commands an event runs, the macros, QuickMenus, K-Board profiles, layouts and events a command uses, the commands of a menu or of a profile… and your own icons, sounds and gestures. To bring it in: Import… in the right-click menu of any of those lists (also in the empty space under the rows), or drop the .kdx on the K-Desktop window. It never overwrites anything: What you already have, the same, is used as it is. If you already have something but with changes, it asks: Add as a copy (it comes in apart, and so does what uses it, so it works as it was exported) or Use mine. A name that already exists gets a number («Greeting 2») and a hotkey you already use is left out. When it is done it opens what came in. From outside: KDesktop.exe --import "file.kdx".

en/k-desktop/events.html.title: Events | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/events.html.summary: Events An event is «when this happens, run these commands». Each event has a trigger, optional conditions and the commands it runs; many triggers also have a «When it ends» part (the program closes, you come back to the PC, the device is removed…) with its own commands. Triggers Trigger When When K-Desktop starts / exits What used to be «Run on startup / on exit» in each command At a time Every day or on some days of the week, at the time you say; or on one day only, if you give it a Day Every so often Every N minutes while K-Desktop runs When a program opens When it opens; «When it ends», when it closes. When Steam opens, audio to the headphones Program in front When its window comes to the front, and when it stops being there PC not in use After some minutes without keyboard or mouse; «When it ends», when you come back Lock, sleep… When the session is locked or unlocked, or the PC sleeps or wakes up Battery or mains When a laptop goes on battery or back on mains power Battery level When the battery goes below a % (or above it); «When it ends», when it is back on the other side Sunrise or sunset At sunrise or sunset where you are, or some minutes before or after (worked out on the PC; See today shows today's). Without a place: «Where you are» in the assistant options or Windows' location File in a folder When a file appears (as soon as it stops growing), changes, is deleted or renamed. The commands get its path in {file} Screen plugged in or out When you plug in or take out a monitor or the TV (also a TV plugged in but not in use yet); the commands get its name in {screen} Call from outside When another computer, Home Assistant or a script asks for it by name, over UDP or the web Drive connected When a USB stick, disk or card is connected (and removed) Network When connecting to a network (or any), or when left without network Device connected When a controller, keyboard, headset or USB gadget is connected (and disconnected) PC usage When the CPU, the graphics card, the memory or the graphics memory (VRAM) goes above (or below) a % for a while Audio device When headphones, a speaker or a microphone are connected, or one becomes the default output or input Calendar event Some minutes before an event, when it starts or when it ends. See Calendar Mail arrives When a mail arrives at one of your accounts, and it can save its attachments. See Mail A Telegram message arrives When yours or a contact's reaches the bot or the account. See Telegram Options Commands: Add command picks commands you already have; New command creates a hidden one named after the event, adds it and opens it so you can put its actions in. Ask an assistant: after the commands, it asks an assistant for something as if you said it (Check the weather and send it to me on Telegram). If the assistant is not on the desktop, nothing happens. Only once: the event is deleted after it runs (if it has commands in When it ends, after those). With At a time and a Day, it is «on Friday at 9, just once». Programmed by an assistant: what you ask for later («at 7 empty the recycle bin», see Tools) shows here as one more event, with who programmed it and what you approved when you asked. You can change or delete it like any other. Conditions (Only if): a list with the same conditions as the If… action (schedule, a program open, the network, the battery, PC usage…), each with The opposite. With several you choose whether all of them must be met or any of them is enough. Each one can be switched off without deleting it and tested (▶) to see whether it is met now. With none, the event always fires. Don't repeat before: if it fires again sooner (in seconds), it does nothing. Loop protection: an event that fires more than 10 times in a minute stops for 10 minutes, and K-Desktop tells you. Each event can be switched off, and run by hand to try it (Test, or KDesktop.exe --event "Name"). The lightning button creates a command that runs it (to give it a hotkey or a voice phrase). When, Only if and Options fold; Only if opens by itself when it has something. Times and dates are set with the arrows, the wheel or by typing them (the date also with its calendar). Calling an event from outside The trigger Call from outside runs when a call with its name arrives. Case and accents do not matter. UDP: event door (port 2501, «Remote control» on) HTTP: POST http://<PC>:2502/api/event X-KD: 1 Authorization: Bearer <token> {"name": "door"} Over UDP it needs Settings → Remote control on with Events allowed (and the key, if there is one, from another computer); over the web, the device needs to be paired (see Phone and remote control).

en/k-desktop/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Requirements Windows 10 (1809 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit. For the assistants' AI (optional): a graphics card with enough memory for the model you choose (a 4B model with vision takes about 5 GB), or another AI server on your network. For the phone remote: the PC and the phone on the same network. The Android app needs Android 5.0 or later. Installing Download KDesktop.exe from the releases. It is a single portable executable: put it wherever you like and open it. .NET does not need to be installed. The first time, a welcome guides you through the basics: language and theme, starting with Windows, the launcher key, voice (it downloads the speech models) and the assistants. Each step changes the setting at once, and you can skip it. To see it again: About → Show the welcome. The first time, K-Desktop registers itself to start with Windows (you can turn that off in Settings → General). It runs as administrator, so its shortcuts also work over programs that run as administrator. Each action that opens something decides whether that program starts as administrator or as a normal user. Your data lives in %APPDATA%\K-Desktop 5: settings, commands, menus, macros, history, backups, logs and the assistants. Your first five minutes Create a command: Commands → New command, give it a name, a hotkey (press the keys or mouse buttons you want) and one or more actions. Press Run to try it. Put it in a menu: in QuickMenu, build the menu that opens at the mouse, with its own shortcut. Talk to it: Settings → Voice downloads the speech models and records your wake word. Then say «K-Desktop, command name». Use your phone: Settings → Web app, scan the QR code with your phone, and your commands are there. Automate: Events runs commands at a time, when a program opens, when you leave the PC… The window The column on the left has every page: Commands, Events, QuickMenu, K-Board, Macros, Assistant (with the assistant module on), History, Settings, Achievements and About. At the bottom, the status icons (paused, remote control, phone, voice, assistant) can be clicked. Closing the window does not close K-Desktop: it stays in the notification area (tray). Right-click its icon to open the launcher, pause it, switch K-Board profiles, show the window or exit. While paused, no command runs (hotkeys, QuickMenus, K-Board, remote…): only the hotkeys to show the window, pause and exit work. Updates K-Desktop looks for new versions at start and every 6 hours. In Settings → Updates you choose what happens when there is one: let you know, or install it by itself (it downloads it and restarts K-Desktop at a moment you are not using it, in a couple of seconds). The Android app is updated from the PC too. Command line KDesktop.exe --menu "Main" opens a QuickMenu (in the running instance) KDesktop.exe --run "Name" runs a command KDesktop.exe --event "Name" runs an event's commands KDesktop.exe --launcher opens the launcher KDesktop.exe --show | --exit shows the window / closes K-Desktop KDesktop.exe --welcome shows the welcome of the first start KDesktop.exe --page macros opens the window on a page (commands, quickmenus, events, macros, kboard, assistant, achievements, stats, settings, about) KDesktop.exe --data "C:\Folder" uses another data folder (an independent instance) KDesktop.exe --no-hooks --no-udp --no-web --no-elevate for diagnostics Any program, script or shortcut can use these to drive the K-Desktop that is already running.

en/k-desktop/macros-kboard.html.title: Macros and K-Board | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/macros-kboard.html.summary: Macros and K-Board Macros A macro stores your keyboard and mouse input with its timing, to repeat it. Macros → New macro, then Record. Do what you want to repeat. Shift + Esc ends the recording (and stops a playback). Edit the steps if you want: press or release a key, type a text, click, move the mouse, turn the wheel, pause… each one with its time. Test plays it once after 3 seconds. Create a command that plays it gives you a command ready to bind to a hotkey. Options: Record mouse movements: when off, only clicks (with their position), the wheel and the keyboard are recorded. Game mode: for games. Clicks do not move the pointer, the mouse is recorded as relative movement (what games read even when they lock the pointer) and keys and clicks are held for a moment so the game sees them. Games with anti-cheat may ignore any simulated input. The Play macro action plays it once or several times, in a loop or at another speed. K-Board K-Board changes what keys, mouse buttons and the wheel do, everywhere or only in the programs you choose: Caps Lock as Ctrl, the Windows key off in games, side buttons that copy and paste… A profile is a set of remaps. Several can be on at the same time. Click a key or button on the drawn keyboard and mouse (or Press key to pick it) and choose what it does: another key, button or the wheel, held down while you hold the original one (it works for modifiers and in games); a text to type, with any keyboard layout (line breaks press Enter); a command (the key no longer reaches the program); nothing (the key is disabled while the profile is on). With modifiers: tick Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win to remap a combination (Ctrl + J) instead of the key itself. Only in these applications: empty = everywhere; with programs, the profile only works while one of them is in front. Always run: also in the programs of Disable in (a game), where the command hotkeys stay off but the keys are still changed. Switch a profile on and off here, from the tray, or from a command with the K-Board action (Create a command that switches this profile on and off).

en/k-desktop/mail.html.title: Mail | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/mail.html.summary: Mail K-Desktop watches your mail accounts and tells you what matters, fires events when a mail arrives, sends mails from your commands, and lets the assistants search, sum up and draft. It is not a mail client: you keep reading your mail where you always do. Accounts Settings → Mail → Add account: the address, a name for the account (Personal, Work… — how the assistant knows it) and how it signs in: With a password (app password). Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password (How to get an app password explains where); other providers, your password. Detect the servers finds IMAP and SMTP by itself; if not, type them. With the connected account: Gmail without an app password, after connecting the account in Settings → Accounts → Google with Gmail ticked. Outlook and Hotmail cannot be connected: Microsoft no longer lets programs sign in with a password. Test checks that it can sign in to IMAP and SMTP and, if not, says why. The password is kept encrypted, only for your user on this PC. Each account also has: What for: Everything (notices, events, assistant and sending) or Send only, an account just for K-Desktop's reports and notices, which only reaches the Allowed addresses (empty: its own address). Notify about: Only important ones, Every new mail or Nothing (only events and the assistant). Mark the mails the assistant reads as read. Important mail and notices Important mail says which mails matter: Senders (addresses, domains like @bank.com, or names) and Words in the subject (invoice, urgent). They are the ones told with Only important ones and the ones the assistant highlights. Notices chooses how a new mail is told: a notification (a click opens the mail on the web: Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo…), an on-screen message (OSD) or an assistant says it (if it is on the desktop; otherwise an OSD). Try a reminder shows one. A mail with a calendar invitation always comes as a notification: clicking it adds the event to the calendar. The important ones can also reach you on Telegram. Actions and events Send mail (action) From one of your accounts, with text with variables and attached files (a screenshot, a report…), or Leave it as a draft Mail arrives (event) When a mail arrives at an account: from someone, with words in the subject, only with attachments or only the important ones. It can save its attachments in a folder (only some kinds: *.pdf). The commands get {mail_subject}, {mail_from}, {mail_snippet}, {mail_attachments}, {mail_paths} (the saved files) and {mail_account} When the electricity bill arrives, save its PDF in the Bills folder and let me know. The assistants With the Assistant module: Check mail and Read a mail («anything from the bank?», «sum up Ana's last mail»), Leave a draft, Send a mail, Tidy up a mail (mark it as read or unread, archive it or move it to the trash, never deleted for good) and Add an invitation to the calendar. Reading never asks; sending always asks; the rest asks until you say «don't ask again» and can be undone. A mail never gives orders: after reading one, the assistant asks before doing anything. In The assistant and mail: Assistants can send (off, they only leave drafts) and Days of mail kept (only the headers and a snippet, to search without asking the server).

en/k-desktop/panels.html.title: Panels | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/panels.html.summary: Panels A panel is a small window on your desktop with figures of your PC: the network, the processor, the memory and the graphics card, always in sight. It stays over the desktop and under your windows (put on the taskbar, in front of it), never takes the focus and does not show in Alt + Tab or on the taskbar. You can have several, each one with its own figures and look. Panels → New panel: it already shows the usual figures in two rows (↑ ↓, CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM and the temperature of the graphics card) and appears at the top right of the main monitor. Drag it with the mouse, from anywhere on it, wherever you like. It remembers where, also on the other monitor and with another resolution. The switch On the desktop (in the list or on the header) shows it or hides it. Figures Figure What it shows Network upload / Network download What the PC sends and receives right now, in kB/s, MB/s or GB/s. Processor (CPU) How busy the processor is, as Task Manager shows it. Memory (RAM) The memory in use. Graphics card (GPU) How busy the graphics card is (games, video, AI). Graphics memory (VRAM) The graphics card's own memory in use. Graphics card temperature In degrees; only with an NVIDIA card. Gap Nothing: an empty cell, so the columns line up the way you want. Add figure adds one (also one it already has: the second one can look different), and you drag them to change the order. On each one you choose: Name shown: its short name on the panel (CPU, ↑…); empty, the usual one. How it looks: Figure only, With a bar (a thin bar under it; for the network, full is the highest speed of the last minute) or With a graph (the last minute, as a small area under it). Look Rows: the figures go in columns of this many rows, from top to bottom. 1 puts them all on one line; as many as figures, one under the other. Text size, Colour of the names, Colour of the figures and Background colour: Automatic follows K-Desktop's theme (the names in its accent colour). Background opacity: 0 % leaves no background, only the text. Every change shows on the panel at once. Options Updates every: from half a second to ten seconds (one second, if you don't change it). Lock the position: dragging it doesn't move it. Let the clicks through (locked): the clicks go to what is under it, as if it were not there. Its menu no longer opens, so you change it from here. Always on top: over every window and the taskbar, even the ones that come up later. It hides by itself while a game or a video fills its screen. Move it to the corner: back to the top right of the main monitor, in case it got lost. Its menu A right click on the panel opens its menu: Lock the position, Always on top, Background opacity, Edit the panel… (opens it here) and Hide. With Show desktop (Win + D) it stays in sight. The tray icon menu also has Panels, to show or hide each one. From a command The action Panel shows, hides, locks or unlocks a panel, or all of them (All panels): give a hotkey to Show or hide and you have it at hand when you want it. Panels are also exported and imported (right click on the list), like commands. K-Desktop only reads what some panel shows, and only while it is on the desktop.

en/k-desktop/quickmenu-launcher.html.title: QuickMenu and launcher | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/quickmenu-launcher.html.summary: QuickMenu and launcher QuickMenu A QuickMenu is a menu with your commands that opens where the mouse is: cascading submenus, icons, an acrylic background and keyboard navigation. Open it from a command with the action Open QuickMenu (give that command a hotkey such as Mouse 4 + Mouse 1), from the phone or with KDesktop.exe --menu "Name". Use it: left click runs and closes, right click runs and keeps the menu open, middle click edits that item. With the keyboard: arrows, Enter and Esc. Close it with Esc or a click outside (K-Desktop's window too). Its hotkey again closes it if the mouse is over the menu; if not, it opens it again where the mouse is. Size: from Compact to Huge, per menu. Editing In QuickMenu, drag commands from the list on the right onto the menu: above, into or below an item. Items can be commands, submenus and separators, each with its own name and icon if you want. Quick command creates a command from a program, a file, a folder or a web page and adds it in one go; you can refine it later in Commands. Double click or F2 renames, Del removes, Alt+↑↓ moves, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo, Ctrl+C / X / V / D copy, cut, paste and duplicate; right click for more. Try it opens the menu as it will look, and the lightning button creates a command that opens it (to give it a hotkey or a voice phrase). The button next to Add to the menu hides that panel for more room. The mouse wheel moves the menu sideways; if it is also taller than the space, the wheel moves it up and down, and Ctrl + wheel sideways. AI menu Create AI menu (under New QuickMenu) creates the QuickMenu «AI» with seven commands for whatever you have selected: Translate and Correct paste the answer over the selection; Summarize, Explain and Reply show it on a sheet. Each one is an Assistant: ask action with {selection} that K-Desktop answers. Read aloud is an Assistant: say with {selection}: K-Desktop reads it with its voice. Translate the screen needs no selection: you pick an area with the mouse, Copy text from the screen reads its text and Assistant: ask translates it on a sheet (with {result}). In each command you can change the text, the answer or choose another assistant. It also creates the command «AI menu», which opens it: give it a hotkey. It needs the Assistant module on and a brain. Launcher The launcher is a search box with its own hotkey (Settings → Launcher). Type part of a name —initials or loose letters work: «cmfy» finds ComfyUI— choose with ↑ ↓ and press Enter. Esc, or the same hotkey, closes it. It finds: Your commands, hidden ones too if you want. Programs of the Start menu, Store apps included. Sums: type 12*3.5 and Enter copies the result. What you copied (Clipboard history): what in the history has what you typed; Enter pastes it where you were. Files and folders: the ones named like what you typed, from the Windows search index and your folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads…). They show a moment later, at the end. Start with ? to search only files (?electricity bill). Enter opens it and Ctrl+Enter opens the folder it is in. The web: when nothing better matches, it offers to search the web (with the search engine you choose). With Most used first, what you use most comes first and shows before you type anything.

en/k-desktop/remote.html.title: Phone and remote control | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/remote.html.summary: Phone and remote control Web app (phone, tablet, any browser) Settings → Web app turns on a small web server on your PC (port 2502 by default). From a phone on the same network you get your commands and menus, the volume and the audio output, a touchpad and keyboard, voice orders and the assistants' chat. It can be installed on the phone as an app (PWA). Turn on Web server. Pair a device: scan the QR code with the phone (or open the link it shows). That is it: the device stays paired until you revoke it in Paired devices. The tabs of the app (Settings opens from the button at the top right): Tab What it has Commands Every command marked Available for remote control, as rows with what it does, its hotkey and where it works. Search, filters by QuickMenu, Favorites and the most used at the top, and Events (the ones fired by name). The result shows on the row itself (✓ or ✕) Menus Your QuickMenus drawn like on the PC: a tap runs and goes back to the first level, holding runs and keeps the menu where it is Touchpad Move the mouse, click, scroll and type on the PC (only with Touchpad and keyboard on) Media What plays on the PC (cover, title, progress and its buttons), the volume, the Volume by app and the audio output Assistant The chat with the assistants, written or spoken (only with the assistant module on) Notes: Nothing works until a device is paired, even from the same PC. Listening on the network needs K-Desktop to run as administrator (as it does by default); otherwise the server only answers this PC. Internet address is optional, only if you come in from outside through a reverse proxy. Accept orders from says where it can be reached from: This PC only, Local network or Internet (what comes through the proxy counts as internet). Pairing is always needed. Holding a command opens its sheet: what it does, all its hotkeys and apps, Favorite, Ask first (it asks before running it from this phone) and Run. Favorites and Ask first are kept per PC. The touchpad One finger moves, a tap clicks, tap and drag (or hold) drags, two fingers scroll, and a two- or three-finger tap is a right or middle click. With Three- and four-finger gestures, like a Windows touchpad: three fingers sideways switch windows, up opens the task view and down shows the desktop; four fingers sideways go to the next virtual desktop. Pinch to zoom zooms in and out like Ctrl + wheel. With the phone on its side the touchpad takes the whole screen. In Settings you can also change the speed, the Acceleration and which Special keys show and in which order. These settings are kept per PC. What plays and the volume Media shows what each program tells Windows it is playing (Spotify, browsers, the Media Player…) with its cover, the progress bar (to move to another point when the player allows it) and its buttons; with several, chips to pick one. Below: the PC's volume, Volume by app (each program with sound, like Windows' volume mixer) and the audio output. In the Android app, What plays, in the notifications shows it as a media notification (also on the lock screen) and the phone's volume keys change the PC's volume while it is there. The assistants on the phone An order written or said on the phone can be answered there: in Settings, Answers play On this phone, On the PC or On both. The PC sends the voice sentence by sentence as it is ready; with On this phone the character on the PC moves its mouth in silence. Keep listening opens the microphone again when it finishes answering. Under each answer, what it did shows as chips («✓ Opened Spotify»). The PC at the top The top shows the PC and how the connection is. Touching it: connect again, change PC (in the Android app) and, with Turn the PC on and off on in Settings → Web app (off by default), Lock, Sleep, Hibernate, Restart and Shut down (these two with 5 seconds to cancel). What the PC sends The Send to phone action and the assistants («send this address to my phone», «tell me on my phone when the download finishes») send a text, a link or a small file (25 MB at most) to your paired devices: all of them, or the one you name. This PC's own browsers do not count. It arrives at once if the app is open, and shows in Received from the PC (the envelope at the top), with buttons to copy, open the link or download the file. If it is not open, K-Desktop keeps it for up to a week and it reaches you as soon as you open it. It goes through no outside server: straight from your PC to your phone. Android app The Android app is the same web app with a few things of its own. Settings → Mobile app → Save the APK…, copy it to the phone and open it (Android asks to allow installing apps from that source). It needs no store: when a phone with an older version connects, the app offers to update itself from the PC. Several PCs. It keeps a list of PCs, each with its addresses (at home and away). It opens the last one at the address that answers; if none answers, it shows My PCs with how each one is, to connect, turn on, rename or forget them. Add PC scans the QR code of Pair a device with the phone's camera, or takes the address typed in. Turn on (see below) and the PC's power from the top. Share → K-Desktop from any app: a text goes to the PC's clipboard, a link asks whether to open it in the PC's browser or copy it, and a file is saved in the PC's Downloads. The PC says so with a notice. Shortcuts: holding the app's icon gives Talk, Touchpad and Switch on the PC. Widget for the home screen with your favorite commands (they run without opening the app) and a button to talk, and Quick Settings tiles: talk, switch on the PC and your first favorite command. The assistants' answers play on the phone also in the background or with the screen off. In its Settings, Messages with the app closed keeps the connection with the PC open even when you close the app, and what the PC sends reaches you as a normal notification (with Open and Copy); what plays on the PC also stays up to date in its notification. Turning it on asks for the notifications and for Android not to put it to sleep to save battery; while it is on, Android shows a fixed «Connection with K-Desktop» notification. It works wherever the phone can reach the PC: at home always, and away only if you have the internet address (proxy). Turning the PC on from the phone With Turn the PC on and off on, the Android app keeps what it needs to turn the PC on while it is off and offers Turn on on the page of PCs. It does two things at once: the Wake-on-LAN signal on the home network and, if you set it, Turn on with a URL (to turn it on away from home). It then waits up to 2 minutes and goes in by itself. For Wake-on-LAN, in Settings → Web app, Check (Wake over the network) says whether a network card can turn the PC on. Usually it needs: Wake-on-LAN on in the BIOS, the card allowed to wake the PC (Device Manager → the card → Power Management, and «Wake on Magic Packet» in Advanced), a cable rather than Wi-Fi, and Windows fast startup off (after «Sleep» it usually works anyway). Turn on with a URL is an address on your network that sends the signal for you, reachable from outside: Method, Request body ({mac} becomes the PC's MAC) and an optional Header for its password (kept encrypted). For example, a Raspberry Pi joined to your proxy by WireGuard, with a small service that only listens on that tunnel: # POST /wol {"mac": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"} with Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN> import json, os, socket, hmac from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer TOKEN = os.environ["WOL_TOKEN"] ALLOWED = {m.upper() for m in os.environ["WOL_MACS"].split(",")} # only your PCs def magic(mac): packet = b"\xff" * 6 + bytes.fromhex(mac.replace(":", "")) * 16 with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) as s: s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_BROADCAST, 1) for port in (9, 7): s.sendto(packet, (os.environ.get("WOL_BROADCAST", "192.168.1.255"), port)) class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_POST(self): if self.path != "/wol" or not hmac.compare_digest(self.headers.get("Authorization", ""), f"Bearer {TOKEN}"): return self.send_response(401) or self.end_headers() body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)) or 0) or b"{}") mac = str(body.get("mac", "")).upper() if mac not in ALLOWED: return self.send_response(400) or self.end_headers() magic(mac) self.send_response(204) self.end_headers() HTTPServer((os.environ.get("WOL_LISTEN", "10.0.0.2"), 8099), Handler).serve_forever() In the proxy, a route /wol to that address, outside any login page, and with a limit of attempts. In K-Desktop: Turn on with a URL https://yourdomain.net/wol, Method POST, Request body {"mac": "{mac}"} and Header Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>. If another of your PCs is on, the app also asks it to turn this one on. UDP Settings → Remote control → UDP server (port 2501) accepts short orders, one per message. Home Assistant, a script, another PC, netcat or a phone app can use it. Order What it does list Answers with your remote commands, numbered A number or a name (or run <name>) Runs that remote command (capitals and accents don't matter) events Answers with the calls your Call from outside events wait for event <name> Fires the events with Call from outside and that name ask <assistant> <text> Asks an active assistant something or gives it an order assistants Answers with the active assistants keys <keys> Presses a key combination (ctrl+c, alt+f4, enter…) type <text> Types a text media play / next / previous / stop Media keys volume up / down / mute Volume show Shows K-Desktop's window help Answers with this list The reply starts with OK or ERROR and goes on in K-Desktop's language. Orders also work in K-Desktop's language (in Spanish: ayuda, lista, ejecutar, eventos, evento, preguntar, teclas, escribir…). If a remote command is called exactly like what you send, the command wins. In programs, use English: it always works, whatever the language. Options: Option What it does Port (UDP) The port; if another program uses it, it says so below Accept orders from This PC only, Local network (VPNs included) or Internet (only with a key, and only signed orders) Key Optional. From another computer it goes in front of each order (mykey list) or orders are signed with it. Not needed from this PC. Generate makes one and copies it Keys and text Allows keys and type (off by default) Hidden commands Hidden remote commands also show in list and can be run Events Allows events and event Assistants Allows ask (off by default) What is not allowed gets no reply, and an address that gets the key wrong several times in a row is ignored for a few minutes. JSON orders (for programs) A program can send the order as JSON and gets the reply as JSON: {"cmd": "run", "arg": "Open Chrome"} {"ok": true, "message": "run: Open Chrome"} {"cmd": "list"} {"ok": true, "commands": ["Open Chrome", "Shut down"]} {"cmd": "ask", "assistant": "lander", "arg": "what's the weather like?"} {"ok": false, "error": "off", "message": "turned off in the remote control options"} cmd is one of the orders in the table (run, list, event, ask, keys, type, media, volume…) and arg what follows it. Errors carry a fixed code in error (notFound, disabled, off, badRequest, noEvent, noAssistant, assistantsOff, notRunning, disabledHere). With a key, the JSON is signed: the key never travels and a captured message can't be replayed. The message is <signature>.<json>, where the signature is the HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON with the key, in hex, and the JSON carries t (the time in Unix seconds; a minute off is fine) and an id that changes with every message: const json = JSON.stringify({ cmd: "run", arg: "Open Chrome", t: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000), id: crypto.randomUUID() }); const signature = crypto.createHmac("sha256", key).update(json).digest("hex"); socket.send(signature + "." + json, 2501, "192.168.1.150"); payload = json.dumps({"cmd": "list", "t": int(time.time()), "id": uuid.uuid4().hex}) signature = hmac.new(key.encode(), payload.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() sock.sendto(f"{signature}.{payload}".encode(), ("192.168.1.150", 2501)) From the internet only signed orders are accepted. For something fuller and paired there is the web API, below. Web API Paired devices can also call the API directly, for instance to run an event: POST http://<PC>:2502/api/event X-KD: 1 Authorization: Bearer <token> {"name": "door"}

en/k-desktop/settings.html.title: Settings, data and privacy | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/settings.html.summary: Settings, data and privacy Settings is organised in foldable groups, with a search box at the top (Ctrl+F): type «volume» or «backup» and it goes there. General Section What it has Appearance Light, dark or system theme; language (Windows', or one of the five built in); website icons; translating General Pause K-Desktop (with its hotkey and sounds); start with Windows, the tray icon and its picture; the hotkeys to show the window and to exit, sounds and startup message Messages and notifications K-Desktop's on-screen messages (OSD): whether they show (off, none does, except countdowns and the progress of what can be stopped), whether countdowns show in a circle in the middle of the screen, a little lower (with a button to try it), which sound plays when a countdown is cancelled with Esc, where they show (clicking on a drawing of the screen), on which monitor, their size, how long they stay, what they do with a film or a game full screen and which groups show (actions, volume and brightness, voice, warnings). Below, the notifications: their sound (the one of all of them; Show notification can choose another or «Global»), whether the achievement ones show and with their sound, on which monitor and corner (also on a drawing), how long they stay and whether they wait until the full-screen thing ends Launcher Its hotkey, what it finds (programs, hidden commands, sums, files, the web) and its order Mouse Hot corners: how long the mouse has to rest in a corner for its command to run. Mouse gestures: on or off, the button to draw (right, middle, Mouse 4 or Mouse 5), show the stroke (the line on the screen and the command that will run) and the programs with no gestures (games, drawing or 3D programs). Block mouse Back / Forward: programs where Mouse 4 and Mouse 5 don't go back or forward. Corners and gestures are chosen in the hotkeys of each command Voice Section What it has Voice Turning voice on or off (off, nothing listens), speech models, microphone, hotkeys to talk and to dictate, and what happens while listening. See Voice Wake words Always-on listening and the words recorded with your voice, whose each one is and its sensitivity Multimedia Section What it has Multimedia Voice orders for music, videos and volume, and the volume step Screenshots Folder (and Open), file name with date, time, program or window title, format (PNG, JPG with its quality, or WebP), wait first (to open a menu), always copy, include the mouse pointer, camera sound and a flash over what was taken Screen recording Folder (and Open), file name (as in screenshots), frames per second (30 or 60), quality (low, normal or high) record the mouse pointer and mark clicks with a circle (yellow for the left button, blue for the others; it is in the video, not on the screen); it is encoded to MP4 (H.264) with the graphics card. For GIF and animated WebP: maximum width (480, 800 or real size; shrunk without distorting) and frames per second (10, 15 or 20) (see Record video in Actions) Audio recording Folder (and Open), file name (as in screenshots), format (WAV, MP3 or Opus: converted when it ends), microphone volume (only in recordings), split long recordings every so many minutes, and Save what just played, which keeps the last seconds in memory so Record audio → Save what just played can save them (nothing is written to disk) Connections Section What it has Remote control The UDP server: port, where from, key and what is allowed. See Phone and remote control Web app The web server, pairing and paired devices, touchpad and keyboard Mobile app Its version and «Save the APK» System Section What it has Disable in Programs where K-Desktop's hotkeys do nothing (games, remote desktops), with a hotkey to add or remove the one in front Magnifier Zoom, shape (rectangular lens, round lens or full screen), size and «Try it»; look: border (none, thin, medium or thick) and its color, colors (normal, inverted or more contrast) and smoothing; behavior: follow the text while you type, Ctrl + wheel changes the zoom while it is on, and turn off by itself after a while without moving the mouse Data The data folder (a link that opens it), export, import and the log; automatic backups (every how many days, how many to keep, folder with Browse and Open, and Back up now) and resetting achievements and statistics Updates Version, Check now, what to do when there is a new one, when to check (when K-Desktop starts, every 6 hours, once a day or once a week) and the installed assistants, each with Update…. A new version is told with a notification; clicking it opens this page The assistant module has its own group: see Assistants. Backups Export saves everything of yours to a .zip: settings, commands, QuickMenus, macros, K-Board profiles, achievements and statistics, wake words, and your own icons, sounds and languages (and the assistants' data). Automatic backups: the same full backup every N days, keeping the last ones, in the folder you choose (safer on another disk, OneDrive or a NAS). Besides, the settings are copied every day. Import restores a backup. The current configuration is saved to the Backups folder first. To take a single thing (a command, a macro, a profile, an event, a QuickMenu, a layout or a text) with what it uses, without touching the rest: export and import one at a time. Languages Five are built in: English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. Extra languages are JSON files in %APPDATA%\K-Desktop 5\Languages. Under Translate, Export template saves the current language: translate the texts, save the file there with the language code (nl.json) and pick it under Language. A file with only some texts (en.json) changes only those. Achievements and statistics Over 100 achievements with animated notifications, and statistics of what you use most. Privacy Speech recognition, wake words, voices and the assistants' AI all run on your PC. Nothing you say or write is sent anywhere. K-Desktop only goes online for what you ask of it: web requests in your commands; the assistants' web, weather and currency tools, and the tools and MCP servers you add yourself; checking for updates, and downloading voices or models. The phone remote talks to the PC over your local network and needs pairing, even from the same PC.

en/k-desktop/telegram.html.title: Telegram | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/telegram.html.summary: Telegram K-Desktop can have its own identity in Telegram: you write to it from your phone to run commands or talk to the assistant, it tells you things (important mails, what your commands send), and you decide who else may write to it and what each person may do. It works without the Assistant module; with it, Telegram is one more way of talking to the assistants. There are two ways, and you can have both at once. Each one has its own page in Settings → Accounts, with its own owner, contacts and options: Telegram Bot Telegram (an account with a number) What it is A bot you create in two minutes with @BotFather A normal Telegram account, best with a phone just for K-Desktop Writes first Only to people who wrote to it before To anybody in its contacts Buttons Yes (commands, Yes / No) No: the options come numbered and you answer with the number or the word Files Up to 50 MB out, 20 MB in Up to 2 GB The bot How to create the bot opens a step-by-step guide: in Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, give it a name and a username ending in «bot», and copy the token it gives you. Settings → Accounts → Telegram Bot → Add a bot, paste the token and Connect. It is checked with Telegram before keeping it, encrypted. Link my account: send the bot the 6-digit code it shows, or open its link, or scan the QR code with your phone. From then on, you are its owner. The account with a number Have the account on a phone (better a real SIM than a virtual number). How to get the api_id and api_hash opens the guide: Telegram asks for your own free «application» at my.telegram.org (API development tools); you copy its two values. Settings → Accounts → Telegram → Log in: the api_id, the api_hash and the number; then the code Telegram sends to the app (or by SMS) and, if the account has two-step verification, its password. The session is kept encrypted, only for your user on this PC. Log out closes it in Telegram too. Link my account: from your own Telegram, send the account the code it shows (find it by its number or username). Telegram watches accounts that write to many people. K-Desktop goes slowly on purpose (a message every little more than a second, and at most 3 people who never wrote to it an hour by default), never writes in bulk, and says on the page if Telegram limits the account for a while. Who can write to it The owner can do everything. Anyone else does what their level allows, also in groups; the level of whoever writes is what counts, not the chat's: Level What they can do Ignore Nothing: their messages are dropped Chat only Talk with the assistant, without tools Chosen commands Run the commands you choose, without AI Tools that only read Chat and tools that change nothing (the weather, the time, searching…) Chosen tools Chat and the tools and commands you choose Like you The same as you on the PC Whatever needs confirming is always asked to you, never to whoever asked: on the PC if you are there, otherwise by Telegram with Yes / No, which expire after 5 minutes without doing anything. Contacts: each one with their level, K-Desktop may write to them, the commands and tools chosen, Who answers them and How it answers them. In the account, Add contact brings someone from its Telegram contacts or adds them By number (also to its contacts in Telegram, so it can write to them first). Someone new who writes waits for your decision: you are told on the PC and on Telegram, with Allow, Ignore and Block. Everyone else: the level of anybody who is not a contact. Above Chat only it needs I understand the risk: anyone who finds it could use your PC. Limits: messages a minute from each person, Only me while I'm gaming (with something full screen it only answers you) and how many messages an hour to people who never wrote. Groups: it only answers when mentioned or when someone replies to its message; each group can be ignored. Blocked: their messages are dropped silently and K-Desktop never writes to them. Commands from Telegram /commands shows the commands that person may run (as buttons in the bot, numbered in the account); writing / and the name runs one too (/game_mode runs «Game mode»: case, accents and spaces don't matter). It answers how it went («✓ Game mode»). Photos, voice notes and files that you and your contacts send are saved in Downloads. Talking to the assistant What is written without / goes to the assistant (with the Assistant module on), with each person's limits: Who answers: the one on screen or one in particular (and each contact can have their own). How it answers: As they write (a voice note is answered with voice, a text with text), With text, With its voice (a voice note in the assistant's own voice) or With text and voice. Voice notes are turned into text on your PC (with the voice models of Settings → Voice); Say what it understood answers first with that text. A photo without text goes to the assistant to look at it. Say what it did puts under the answer what it did («✓ Opened Spotify»). Texts from others are data, not orders: in a group, with a forwarded message or a file from someone else, anything that acts asks you first. Whoever is not the owner has a conversation of their own and does not see the assistant's memory. Which one writes It answers by where it was written to: to the bot, the bot; to the account, the account. To write first, Automatic uses the account when that person is its owner or one of its contacts, and otherwise the bot. The Send via Telegram action has With (Automatic, The bot, The account), and you can tell the assistant «by the bot» or «by the account». Important mails: in Telegram notices of each page; if both have it on, it comes once, by the account. Actions, events and tools Send via Telegram (action) To you or a contact: a text with variables, a file, a screenshot or what is on the clipboard. Who got it goes into {result} A Telegram message arrives (event) Only your messages or someone's, with some words, of a kind (text, voice note, photo or file). The commands get {telegram_text}, {telegram_from}, {telegram_file} and {telegram_id} Assistant tools Send a Telegram message, Send a file by Telegram (a file, a screenshot or the last one that arrived) and Read Telegram (the last messages of a chat). Sending to you asks until you say «don't ask again»; to anyone else, always When I send «note …» from my phone, add it to my notes.

en/k-desktop/texts.html.title: Texts | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/texts.html.summary: Texts In Texts you keep short abbreviations that K-Desktop swaps for a longer text when you type them in any program: your signature, your address, an answer you keep repeating. Texts → New text. Type the abbreviation (sig) and the text that replaces it. In any program, type the prefix and the abbreviation (;sig): it is erased and the text appears. Try each one in the Try it box on the same page. Inside K-Desktop they are only written there, never while you edit them. Options Write as you type: turns every text on or off at once. Each text also has its own On switch, in the list and on its card. Prefix: goes before every abbreviation (; by default) so normal writing never sets one off. You can change it or leave it empty; without a prefix, an abbreviation only goes off as a whole word (ok does not go off inside book). In each text, Text, Try it, Options and Notes fold, and stay as you leave them from one text to the next. Only in these applications (in Options): empty, the text works everywhere. With applications, it only goes off with one of them in front, also if they are in Disable in. So you can have the same abbreviation with one text for e-mail and another for the rest: the application's one wins there. In the list, under each text, you can see where it works, as in K-Board. Notes: anything you want to jot down about the text; it is never written. When it goes off As soon as you finish typing the abbreviation. If another abbreviation starts the same (;fe and ;fecha), the short one waits for Space, Tab or Enter. With Space, the space stays after the text. Under the abbreviation you can see how yours goes off. Typing the abbreviation in capitals (;SIG) writes the text in capitals; with the first letter in capitals (;Sig), the text starts with a capital. It does not go off in password boxes, in full-screen games or films, in the programs of Disable in, or while K-Desktop is paused. What the text can hold Type { in the text to pick: Variable What it puts {cursor} Nothing: leaves the cursor there at the end (for example {cursor}) {date} Today's date (2026-10-29) {time} The time (09:30:05) {clipboard} The copied text {clipboard:2} What was copied before the last one (:3, :4… further back) Short texts are typed. Long ones, or with several lines, are pasted (so a line break does not send the message in a chat) and what you had copied goes back where it was.

en/k-desktop/voice.html.title: Voice | K-Desktop
en/k-desktop/voice.html.summary: Voice K-Desktop understands spoken orders on your PC: neither the audio nor the text leaves it, and no internet is needed. Setting it up Settings → Voice → Voice models → Download. They are downloaded once: Parakeet (speech to text, many languages), Silero (detects when you speak), the wake-word detector and EmbeddingGemma (finds the command by its meaning). Loaded, they take about 700 MB of RAM; they can be freed after some minutes unused (not Parakeet while a wake word is being listened for: that way it checks the word at once). Choose the microphone (or the Windows default). Record a wake word (Settings → Wake words → Add word) or set a hotkey to talk. Talking to it Hotkey: hold it while you say what to do («open the recycle bin»), or tap it once and speak: it ends when you stop talking. Pressing it again ends sooner; Esc cancels. Wake word: with Always-on listening, say the word and the order together («K-Desktop, open the browser»), or just the word and wait for «Listening…». The command you name runs. It is found by its name (also when the recognition gets it a little wrong) or by its meaning («put some music on» finds your «Spotify» command). You can teach a command more phrases. Wake words In Settings → Wake words you record your own word with your voice, in a few seconds, with a small wizard: some silence, the word several times, and a bit of normal speech so it learns what is not the word. Each word belongs to K-Desktop (your commands), to an assistant, or to nobody (not listened to). Sensitivity: further right catches it more easily, but it may also go off without you saying it. Try tells you how it does. Answer faster: when the detector has no doubt, it answers without checking with Parakeet. Nothing shows (no «Listening…», no sound, no music turned down) until it has checked it really was the word. Said in the middle of a sentence («I was showing my brother the Lander») it takes it you are talking about it, not to it, and does nothing. While you speak Ignore what the PC is playing: echo cancellation takes music and films out of the microphone, so it understands you even while something plays. Turn the volume down while you speak: the other programs go down until the order is over (for an assistant, until it has finished answering). Sound when listening. Music, videos and volume Settings → Multimedia: orders like «play», «pause», «next», «turn the volume up», «volume to 30» work without creating any command, in any of the installed languages. They use the media keys, so they work with any player that listens to them: music, the browser, a film («pause the movie»). Dictation The Dictate action (and its own hotkey in Settings → Voice) types what you say where the cursor is, without AI. Say «new line», «new paragraph», «delete that» or «stop dictating»; it also ends after a few seconds of silence or with Esc. With Start dictation by voice on (Settings → Voice, under the dictation hotkey), you can also start it as a voice order: «start dictating», «dictation mode», «write what I say».

en/sdk/gestures.html.title: Gestures | K-Desktop
en/sdk/gestures.html.summary: Gestures The module asks the assistant for gestures: what it wants to achieve, never how. Each assistant decides how to perform them —the Lander shoots the minimise button, Kobii throws a ball at it, Kumo pokes it—. An assistant that only knows Communicate and React already works: for the rest the module shows the bubble and does the action itself. public bool CanPerform(Gesture gesture) => gesture.Kind is GestureKind.Communicate or GestureKind.React; public async Task<GestureOutcome> PerformAsync(Gesture gesture, IGestureContext ctx, CancellationToken ct) { … } List the ones it knows in traits.gestures of its manifest. CanPerform says whether it can do one now (yes by default); GestureOutcome.NotPerformed says no just as well. Never throw. The gestures Gesture What it asks for PointAt(Place) Point at a window, a point, an area, the tray or the clock (a spotlight, an arm…) GoTo(Place) Go somewhere (fly, walk, teleport) PressButton(Window, Button, ButtonBounds) Press a caption button (minimise, maximise/restore, close) MoveWindow(Window, Destination) Move a window there (a maximised one arrives already restored by a PressButton(Restore) before) ActivateWindow(Window) Bring a window to the front (perch on it, knock on the door…) WaitForWindow(Process, Title) Something was just opened: wait for its window. ctx.Appeared gives it (or null) Mark(Place, Duration, Text) Leave a mark somewhere for a while (a beacon, a flag, an alarm clock), with an optional label Scan(Area) Sweep an area (a screenshot, reading the screen) Typing(Window) Pretend to type into a window (keys or text are being sent to it) Communicate(Text, Icon) Stay visible while the host shows the text in the bubble. Icon says what it is about when known (clock, folder, web, volume, power…; show the ones you do not know without a picture) React(Reaction) A short reaction: Success, Warning, Failure, Celebration, with its context Announce(Reason, Cursor, UserAway) Catch the user's eye before saying something on its own The commands of the user When the user asks an assistant to run a K-Desktop command, each action arrives as one or several gestures: minimise → PressButton(Minimize), place a window → MoveWindow with the exact target, a maximised one first PressButton(Restore)… Call ctx.Commit() at the instant of the effect (when the shot hits): the action happens right then, and ctx.Committed tells you whether it went well. Or do it yourself (Windows.TryMove frame by frame) and return PerformedSelf: K-Desktop then sets it to the pixel. What you cannot do (CanPerform false) the host shows with the bubble while K-Desktop does it. You have ctx.TimeLeft: if you run over, fail or do not answer, K-Desktop does it anyway and asks you for a React(Warning). An order is never left half done; the token fires when the time is up or the user says «stop». ctx.Speed is the speed the user chose (Showy, Normal, Fast): in Fast, Commit within half a second. ctx.Step and ctx.StepCount say which step of the order it is. if (gesture is Gesture.PressButton press) { // FlyNextToAsync and ShootAsync are the assistant's own animations. await FlyNextToAsync(press.ButtonBounds, ctx.TimeLeft, ct); await ShootAsync(press.ButtonBounds, ct); ctx.Commit(); // the window minimises now, on impact return await ctx.Committed ? GestureOutcome.Committed : GestureOutcome.NotPerformed; } With Also show the commands you launch on, commands run by other means (a hotkey, a QuickMenu, the phone) reach you as gestures too, always in Fast: they are only decoration, nothing waits for them and their Commit does nothing. The tools of the AI What the AI's tools do reaches you as gestures too, with ctx.Step 0: Tool Gesture A timer Mark by the clock (Place.Clock) with the time it rings; removing it → PointAt(Place.Clock) Opening a website, a search, a program or a file WaitForWindow, right before opening it What's playing, controlling the music GoTo(Place.Tray) «Tell me when … closes» Mark on that window Rewriting a text and pasting it Typing in that window Reading the screen Scan of what was read JSON tools can ask for one with "gesture". They are only decoration: the tool never waits for you, Commit does nothing, a step of an order takes their place and a new one replaces the one before. What you cannot do is not shown. Catching the eye Before saying something on its own (a timer ringing, a «tell me when» coming true, Assistant: say with «Go towards the mouse» ticked) the host asks for Announce: walk up to the mouse, wave, blink… Reason says why (Timer, Watch, Message), Cursor where the mouse was (or null) and UserAway how many seconds without keyboard or mouse (the longer, the bigger it may be: maybe they are not looking). The host waits for you, ctx.TimeLeft at most (about 2 s, 3 in Showy and half a second in Fast), and then talks with Communicate: finish as soon as you have caught the eye. There is nothing to commit. Reactions Gesture.React carries Context (ReactionContext), filled in by the host: Source Order (a command or a K-Desktop action), Tool (a timer, a note, the web…), Notice (something it says on its own), User (what the user says about it: «thanks», «well done» → Celebration; «that's wrong» → Failure), or Unknown Streak How many in a row of the same kind (1 the first; back to 1 with another kind or after half an hour) FirstToday The first one today What What it was when known (set_timer, run_command, timer, praise…) The host reacts once per order, when the answer is ready: something done and nothing failed → Success; done but something failed → Warning; nothing done and something failed → Failure. Only looking something up (the time, the weather) does not react. Use it with Variety<T> not to react the same way every time: something bigger the first time today or on a long streak, more downcast at the third failure in a row.

en/sdk/getting-started.html.title: With code | K-Desktop
en/sdk/getting-started.html.summary: With code An assistant with code is a .NET class library (net10.0-windows, WPF) that implements IAssistant from the SDK. The SDK is always provided by K-Desktop: a package never carries it. Starting from the template You need the .NET 10 SDK. The template and the SDK come from NuGet (KDesktop.Assistant.Templates, KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk): dotnet new install KDesktop.Assistant.Templates dotnet new kdassistant -n MyAssistant --authorName "Me" cd MyAssistant dotnet build # → bin\Debug\…\myassistant-1.0.0.kai To build against a clone of the K-Desktop repository instead (to try a change in the SDK), add --sdk "<K-Desktop>\src\KDesktop.Assistant.Sdk". MyAssistant.cs The class that implements IAssistant: it draws itself, has a click area and knows Communicate, React and Announce Package\assistant.json The manifest Package\… Everything else that goes into the package as it is: icon.png, settings.json, panel.json, persona\, voice\, assets\ Every build leaves the package in bin\…\package\ exactly as it is installed and, next to it, the .kai (signed, if you have a key: see Signing). Trying it without installing KDesktop.exe --assistant-dev "<project folder>" It loads the newest bin\…\package (a copy, so you can keep building) and reloads it on every build. If K-Desktop is open with the same data folder it connects to it; otherwise it works alone. The log is Logs\assistant.log in the data folder. KDesktop.exe --assistant --exit closes it. The smallest assistant Only a few members are required; every other one has a default that does nothing (or says no). public sealed class MyAssistant : IAssistant { private IAssistantHost _host = null!; private ISurface _surface = null!; private IHitArea _hit = null!; private Point _at; private bool _dirty = true; public Point? BubbleAnchor => new Point(_at.X, _at.Y - 20); public void Attach(IAssistantHost host) { _host = host; _surface = host.Rendering.CreateSurface(); _hit = host.Pointer.CreateHitArea(); } public void Enter(EntranceKind how) { var work = _host.World.Current.PrimaryMonitor?.WorkArea ?? new PixelRect(0, 0, 800, 600); _at = new Point(work.Right - 200, work.Bottom - 24); } public Task ExitAsync(ExitKind why, CancellationToken ct) => Task.CompletedTask; public double Tick(TickInfo tick) { if (_dirty) { _dirty = false; var area = new PixelRect((int)_at.X - 24, (int)_at.Y - 24, (int)_at.X + 24, (int)_at.Y + 24); _surface.Present(area, dc => dc.DrawEllipse(Brushes.MediumPurple, null, _at, 18, 18)); _hit.Place(new HitShape.Ellipse(area)); } return 30; // nothing moves: sleep (anything that matters calls RequestTick) } public async Task<GestureOutcome> PerformAsync(Gesture gesture, IGestureContext ctx, CancellationToken ct) { if (gesture is Gesture.Communicate) try { await Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct); } catch (OperationCanceledException) { } return GestureOutcome.Committed; } public void SetState(AssistantState state, StateDetail detail) { } public void Dispose() { _hit.Dispose(); _surface.Dispose(); } } Rules Everything is called on the host's engine thread, and awaits come back to it. Nothing needs locking; never block that thread. Tick returns how long it may sleep: at rest, seconds; while animating, Rendering.FrameInterval. Only draw (Present) when something changes: the last frame stays on screen, even if the GPU is lost or a full-screen game ends. Coordinates are physical pixels of the virtual screen. For sizes, the monitor's scaling (MonitorInfo.DpiScale). You are not alone: other assistants may be on the desktop at the same time, in the same process and on the same layer. Do not take the whole screen; World.Others says where the others are. What reaches you (gestures, orders, extras, settings) is yours alone. Never throw to say no: return GestureOutcome.NotPerformed. An exception is logged; several in a row unload the assistant.
